causal_research.flaw_origin: The smallest public first-write of the raw_proxy sink is PR #23330 member 657cf465b0cf10af211d9ff582c340e36f076ac0 (parent 068831553eec9312b62a9ee7ba6f29ed01472ec8), which added POST /gateway/proxy/{endpoint_name}/{path:path} and provider._proxy that forwards the caller path to send_request(base_url=self._api_base|self.base_url). That commit's parent tree has no raw_proxy/_proxy. GitHub then squash-merged the PR onto master as 96b7d900e14227e0821981409d86f5fb6c59b386, first released in v3.13.0rc0/v3.13.0. Unvalidated auth_config storage is older (5afc02ee, v3.8.0) and is a precondition, not the commit that first wrote this SSRF mechanism.
causal_research.remaining_gap: No public fix SHA through clone HEAD ce53bdf8a101fa031a1fce84c762c87a607ab7d9; GHSA first_patched_version remains null and v3.16.0 still ships the proxy sink.

potential_fix.approach: Reject non-http(s) and non-global/metadata api_base values in _create_gateway_secret and _update_gateway_secret by calling _validate_webhook_url (or a gateway-specific equivalent). Re-validate and pin the resolved peer at send_proxy_request/_aiohttp_post time, and reject path traversal. Add CreateGatewaySecret to BEFORE_REQUEST_HANDLERS with a dedicated create/manage permission so read-only users cannot plant a secret.
potential_fix.rationale: The SSRF is the missing destination check on a user-controlled URL that the proxy then fetches. The webhook guard already encodes the required IP policy and was present on the BIC parent (06883155 mlflow/utils/validation.py:733) but unused on this path. Create-time validation plus request-time pinning closes stored-URL and DNS-rebinding gaps; the missing BEFORE_REQUEST entry is the privilege amplifier named in the advisory.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Mechanism: CVE-2026-35041 / GHSA-cjw9-ghj4-fwxf is a ReDoS (CWE-1333) in nearform/fast-jwt. When an allowed* verification option (allowedAud and the sibling allowedJti/allowedIss/allowedSub/allowedNonce) is configured with a RegExp, verification evaluates attacker-controlled claim strings against it via `allowed.some(a => a.test(v))` (validateClaimValues in src/verifier.js; same pattern at v5.0.0 and v6.2.0), so a crafted JWT claim triggers catastrophic backtracking and CPU exhaustion. Lineage/BIC: the vulnerable matcher is present in the repository's first source commit, 51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790 'feat(wip): Initial version.' (2020-01-15 19:44:15 +0100, author and committer both Shogun <shogun@cowtech.it>, i.e. Paolo Insogna / GitHub ShogunPanda). That commit adds src/verifier.js already containing ensureStringClaimMatcher and `allowed.some(a => a.test(value))`; its parent 5063678a36ff118da9671f1f1df3d67cc95d1169 'feat: Initial commit.' is scaffolding only (.eslintrc.js, .github/workflows/ci.yml, .gitignore, CHANGELOG.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, LICENSE.md, package.json, prettier.config.js, yarn.lock) with no src/ tree, verified with git ls-tree. So 51fe1ea is the true minimal BIC (first write, parent lacks the pattern). Later commits are refactors, not first writes: b1d71ed6 (#67, 2021-03-08, Shogun) switched string allowed values to exact equality but kept the RegExp .test path; 18d25904 (#593, 2026-04-09, Antonio Attanasio) reset lastIndex before r.test for the sibling CVE-2026-35040 and is not the BIC here. The advisory's affected range '>= 5.0.0, < 6.2.1' traces to the v5.x validation rewrite (c4d4580 feat!: align claim validation to specification, released as v5.0.0 on 2024-11-20); independent tag inspection confirms the identical vulnerable `allowed.some(a => a.test(v))` is still present at v5.0.0 and v6.2.0, so the 5.0.0 lower bound is conservative/editorial and the underlying code dates to 2020. Fix: b0be0ca161593836a153d5180ca5358ad9b5de94 (#595, 2026-04-09, author Antonio Attanasio <antonio.attanasio@nearform.com>) adds checkForUnsafeRegExp, which runs the newly added safe-regex2 dependency (^5.1.0) over RegExp values in allowedJti/allowedAud/allowedIss/allowedSub/allowedNonce and emits a FAST_JWT_UNSAFE_REGEXP process warning; it does not reject or block the unsafe RegExp, so the ReDoS surface remains unless the operator acts on the warning. First release containing the fix: v6.2.1 (tag 6b13fe9 'Release v6.2.1 (#600)', b0be0ca verified as ancestor via git merge-base --is-ancestor). Affected: >= 5.0.0, < 6.2.1. AI role on BIC: NOT_AI. The BIC is a 2020 initial commit by a named human maintainer, written before modern AI pair-programming trailer conventions existed; the raw commit object carries no Co-Authored-By, no 'Generated with', no Copilot/Claude/Cursor markers, and author=committer. AI-authored commits do appear later in the repo (e.g. e4cbab3, 378422c, Copilot) but they are unrelated to this BIC and were never used for inverse search. Verdict preserved: NOT_AI.

First-write conflict resolved: the true BIC is 70685406 (pGrovesy, 2020-04-27, 'can now pull the PACK meta data from the push, next zlib deflate for inspection'), which first wrote `lastIndexOf('PACK')` in lib/processors/parsePush.js (+42 lines); its single parent 572e98d already held lib/processors/parsePush.js as a stub, but `git grep lastIndexOf('PACK')` on the parent returns nothing, and pickaxe `-S "lastIndexOf('PACK')"` first-hits 70685406. Fernando's 8cec7591 (grovesy, 2020-05-31, 'wip') is NOT the origin: it is a later 166-line re-add/refactor of the same parser at a new path server/src/node_modules/proxy/processors/push-action/parsePush.js (same `lastIndexOf('PACK')` line, new tree); `--follow` on the server path shows 8cec7591 as its first write, while `--follow` on lib/processors/parsePush.js traces the PACK logic back to 70685406. causal_research.bug_semantics: CVE-2025-71372 / GHSA-rrxm-2pvv-m66x: picklescan's blocklist-based scanner missed the numpy.f2py module. A crafted pickle whose REDUCE/global import references numpy.f2py.crackfortran.getlincoef (or _eval_length), helpers that eval() arbitrary strings, was not classified Dangerous by the scanner, so consumers gating on dangerous findings (or, in the earliest releases, any finding at all) passed malicious pickles; VulnCheck credits reporters ac0d3r and Lyutoon. Verified lineage: scanner first written in c1d5abd (2022-09-04, 'Implement Pickle scanner'); parent 6a76b8c3 ('Add boilerplate', 2022-09-03) contains no scanner.py and no pickle-global detection, so the detection-gap BIC is the scanner first-write itself. Per-module checks: git log -S'numpy.f2py' over full history finds exactly one commit, the fix; none of the intermediate list-expansion commits (9c31e17, 1c86244, 5adf310, 62e76cf #40, 7f994d6 #47, 1931c2d #49, 28a7b4e #50, d3273f4 #52) added numpy.f2py. Fix: 70c1c6c ('Fix various vulnerabilities', PR #53, 2025-12-26) adds _unsafe_globals['numpy.f2py']='*' and generalizes the wildcard parent-module check to ANY ancestor module (not just the first path segment), which is what makes the numpy.f2py.crackfortran submodule match; this commit is exactly tag v0.0.33, so first fixed release v0.0.33 (2025-12-26), affected boundary < 0.0.33 (all releases from initial v0.0.2, 2022-09-06, through v0.0.32, 2025-11-13), consistent with the CVE primary record. The entry is still present at HEAD (v1.0.5). torch/lib2to3 prose in the source report belongs to sibling picklescan advisories and was excluded; this case's module is numpy.f2py only. AI role: none on the BIC - named maintainer Matthieu Maitre, 2022-09-04 GitHub-noreply authorship, no AI/co-author trailers anywhere in the 2022 history (repo's first Claude-related tooling commits appear only 2026-08, long after); supplied NOT_AI verdict retained.

Lineage (verified locally in mmaitre314/picklescan): BIC c1d5abd 'Implement Pickle scanner' (2022-09-04, Matthieu Maitre) is the first write of src/picklescan/scanner.py (git A status) with the denylist; parent 6a76b8c is boilerplate-only (.gitignore/LICENSE/README.md/conda.yaml/requirements.txt/setup.cfg, no src tree), so the vulnerable state (scanner exists, omits _operator.methodcaller) is first introduced at c1d5abd. Module coverage verified at each candidate: '_operator' appears nowhere in scanner.py at c1d5abd, at 108b060 (2023-12-16 'Add attrgetter', first operator coverage as 'operator': 'attrgetter'), at d3273f4 (v0.0.32, same scalar attrgetter-only entry), or at 70c1c6c (v0.0.33, #53) which expanded 'operator' to {attrgetter, itemgetter, methodcaller} while still lacking '_operator' - the archive's asymmetric-alias nomination 70c1c6c is therefore NOT the first defect: its parent already contained the identical _operator.methodcaller miss (and additionally missed operator.methodcaller), so #53 was a coverage expansion, not an introduction; per corpus convention for never-present entries the gap originates at scanner inception. Commit cf1592582e965f16412d644588297eaf45911ae6 (2011-04-20, Angela Schreiber, also JCR-2887) is a MOVE from jackrabbit-jcr-commons/.../privilege/ to jackrabbit-spi-commons/.../privilege/, not a first write: the destination path is absent only because the file was relocated; its parent d6718b470b46869510f40f9dd547dd8fa2c817d3 still contains the same unsafe createFactory() at jackrabbit-jcr-commons/src/main/java/org/apache/jackrabbit/commons/privilege/PrivilegeXmlHandler.java (lines 96-104). causal_research.bug_semantics: Independently verified against the local encode/starlette clone (full commit objects). BIC 97257515 ('Thread pool is no longer used for files in memory', PR #933, 2020-05-06, author 云中君/AberSheeran) added the `_in_memory` property and changed UploadFile.write to `if self._in_memory: self.file.write(data)` (synchronous) else `run_in_threadpool`. causal_research.bug_semantics: Netty DNS CNAME cache poisoning / cross-domain cache reuse (CVE-2026-45674 / GHSA-676x-f7gg-47vc): the resolver cached CNAME mappings resolved during a lookup without restricting them to the queried domain, so a CNAME observed while resolving one name could be served for a different queried domain (cache-poisoning / resolution-integrity defect). OSV-listed a41f7b289c/f05f765d81 are maven-release-plugin version bumps for 4.2.15/4.1.135, not the code fix. AI: both BIC and fix are named-human Netty maintainer commits (Norman Maurer) with no AI markers. NOT_AI.

Mechanism: picklescan flags a pickle REDUCE global only when module:function appears in its static blocklist (scanner.py _unsafe_globals/_suspicious_globals); torch.utils._config_module.ConfigModule.load_config was absent from the list until the fix, so a crafted pickle calling ConfigModule.load_config(None, inner_pickle_bytes) passed the scan as clean while pickle.load() reached torch's load_config, which pickle.loads() the bytes argument (verified in torch v2.2.2 torch/utils/_config_module.py) and executes the embedded payload -> RCE, per the advisory PoC and the fix comment 'allows storing a pickle inside a pickle'. Timing: the vulnerable callable entered the torch dependency in the 2.2 series (file present at tag v2.2.2, 404 at v2.1.2), i.e. Dec 2023 onward; picklescan's torch coverage (f98f9bd, 2022-10-01) and dangerous torch-callable entries (62e76cf, 2025-04-06: torch.serialization.load, torch._inductor.codecache.compile_file) never included _config_module, so the omission gap existed from scanner inception for any torch>=2.2 load environment. causal_research.bug_semantics: Mechanism: Apache ActiveMQ exposes a FactoryFinder-based classpath resource loader at two authenticated entry points -- the Web console queue-browse servlet and the STOMP TRANSFORMATION translation header. getMessageBuilder()/getMessageRenderer() (QueueBrowseServlet, BIC d754e76c 2006-03-28) and ProtocolConverter.findTranslator() (STOMP, BIC 2b5608f7 2008-01-16, AMQ-943) both pass attacker-controlled key strings into Class.forName via FactoryFinder.newInstance(style) with raw path+key concatenation, allowing authenticated input to escape the META-INF services directory -> classpath resource/class loading abuse, chained for exploit. Minimal BIC: d754e76c (verified local clone, first write A/new file, parent 3263205bf lacks QueueBrowseServlet AND web/view MessageRenderer services). Stomp BIC is second endpoint, same mechanism, later lineage. Windows path-separator repair landed after: main bedb1080 (#1831, 2026-03-26) + branch backports c2f8f19f (#1836 6.2.x) and 422dbf7b (#1837 5.19.x), all authored Christopher L. Shannon. causal_research.bug_semantics: Mechanism: UniqueSecurityAnnotationScanner.findClosestMethodAnnotations fails to locate @PreAuthorize on a method inherited through an unbounded generic supertype when the subclass does not redeclare the method, so scan() returns null and the PreAuthorize expression is never built (CWE-863 authorization bypass, HIGH per spring.io advisory, credited to Avgustin Marinov). BIC verified by local git: 626610a 'Polish Annotation API' (2024-08-29) is the creation commit of UniqueSecurityAnnotationScanner.java; diff-tree against parent cc6de8fa shows the file added (status A) together with the rest of the scanner family replacing the AnnotationSynthesizer-based lookup, so the vulnerable traversal is co-extensive with the file itself. The dossier's BIC dc2e1af (gh-16751, authored 2025-01-08, committed 2025-03-17, first tag 6.4.4; parent 4993fa86 verified) is the immediate parent of the fixed line: its diff adds hasSameGenericTypeParameters using ResolvableType.forMethodParameter(candidateMethod, i, sourceDeclaringClass).resolve(). However the fix's own regression scenario (gh-17898: GenericInterfaceImpl with no redeclared processOneAndTwo) already fails on the pre-BIC traversal, which matched overrides only via exact erased signatures getDeclaredMethod(name, Long, Object) against the interface method erased to (Object, Object); the raw 6.4.0 blob shows that original lookup, and the vendor affected range starting at 6.4.0 corroborates it. dc2e1af therefore changed the miss mechanism (unresolved type variable makes .resolve() return null, failing the parameter comparison) rather than introducing the vulnerable class, and is not the true BIC. Minimal fix: e5694ac 'Fallback to Object When Determining Overridden Methods' (gh-17898, 2025-09-15) changes exactly one main-code line, .resolve() to .toClass(), so unresolvable type variables fall back to Object and match the erased root parameter type; it adds the regression test scanWhenAnnotationOnParameterizedUndeclaredMethodAndThenLocates. Merge d0f93fa6d8338149943ae640c53db07de827867f ('Merge branch 6.4.x into 6.5.x', 2025-09-15, second parent = e5694ac) carries the fix into 6.5.x. AI exclusion rests on positive evidence, not trailer absence: calibrating the 6.4.4..e5694ac window shows 297 non-merge commits of which 227 carry trailers and all 227 are Signed-off-by; a repo-wide 2025 body census finds zero Co-authored-by/Generated-with markers, so this repo has no AI-marker convention and marker absence is non-informative. Positive human signals: all four lineage commits are authored by Josh Cummings (2024 creation commit GPG-signed with personal gmail; 2025 commits under his GitHub noreply identity); each closes a distinct upstream issue (gh-16751, gh-17143, gh-17898) in the repo's human-issue workflow; the fix was authored and committed within 15 minutes on 2025-09-15 during same-day security-release cadence with the 6.5.x merge 15 minutes later; Josh has 22 commits in the window with zero AI-marker bodies; the BIC itself (2024-08-29) predates the dossier's 2025 coverage window so the missing-2025-trailer concern does not apply. No AI co-author evidence exists anywhere in the lineage. causal_research.bug_semantics: CVE-2025-66490 (GHSA-gm3x-23wp-hc2c, traefik/traefik): HTTP path-prefix routing trusts the encoded request path. Local-clone verified: BIC b23b2611 (Add non regex pathPrefix, Emile Vauge, 2017-12-19) replaces gorilla/mux PathPrefix with a lightweight prefixMatcher that matches strings.HasPrefix(r.URL.Path, prefix) on the escaped/encoded path and adds no rejection of encoded reserved characters; parent 877770f7 routes via gorilla/mux PathPrefix (same encoded-path view), so the encoded-view predicate itself predates the BIC, but the new matcher is the surviving vulnerable first-write and the advisory repair targets this matcher era. Fix 4d7d627 (Reject suspicious encoded characters, Romain, 2025-12-04, Co-authored-by Kevin Pollet) adds EncodedCharacters config plus denyEncodedCharacters middleware scanning req.URL.EscapedPath and returning 400 for disallowed encodings (slashes, backslash, null, semicolon, percent, question mark, hash). Note: the fix is config-gated with backward-compatible defaults allowing all encodings unless operators set AllowEncoded* = false, i.e. an opt-in mitigation rather than a universal hard default.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Mechanism: picklescan detects malicious pickles via a hand-maintained denylist of dangerous importable callables; CVE-2025-71353/GHSA-86cj-95qr-2p4f is a missed-entry flaw - a pickle whose REDUCE references torch._dynamo.guards.GuardBuilder.get (code execution gadget) was never flagged because the module was absent from the denylist until the Aug 2025 fix. Lineage (verified locally in mmaitre314/picklescan): BIC c1d5abd (2022-09-04, Matthieu Maitre, 'Implement Pickle scanner') first writes src/picklescan/scanner.py (A-status) and its denylist (named _suspicious_globals at inception, later split/renamed _unsafe_globals; the archive's '_unsafe_globals at inception' wording is anachronistic). Parent 6a76b8c 'Add boilerplate' contains only .gitignore/LICENSE/README/conda.yaml/requirements.txt/setup.cfg - no src tree, no scanner, so the vulnerable state (scanner exists but omits the callable) is first introduced at c1d5abd and persists unchanged through v0.0.27. The omission only became material to torch-internal gadget scope at 93764d6 (2025-03-02, Trevor Madge/Sonatype, 'Merge commit from fork', Co-authored-by Matthieu Maitre), the first denylist expansion adding torch.* entries (torch.serialization 'load', torch._inductor.codecache 'compile_file') while GuardBuilder.get (public in torch 2.x, well before Mar 2025) stayed unlisted; #40 (62e76cf, 2025-04-06) re-sorted the list and added numpy._core but added no torch module. Fix: 7f994d6 (2025-08-22, Matthieu Maitre, PR #47 'Missing detection when calling PyTorch functions', message 'Address security advisories') is a squash of a multi-advisory repair (8 GHSA reproducer pickles incl. GHSA-86cj-95qr-2p4f.pkl plus unrelated black reformatting); its atomic per-module change adds 'torch._dynamo.guards': {'GuardBuilder.get'} plus six other torch.* gadget entries. Release boundary: v0.0.28 tag points exactly at 7f994d6 (first fixed release, 2025-08-22, matching CVE datePublic); v0.0.27 = 58983e1 (2025-08-09) is the last affected release, consistent with CVE 'lessThan 0.0.28'. No earlier commit on any ref contains GuardBuilder (later #53 70c1c6c 2025-12-26 only touched pydoc and preserved this entry). AI evidence on BIC: positive NOT_AI - named human maintainer authored the scanner in 2022; commit message has no AI trailers; repo calibration shows AI-assisted commits are explicitly labeled when they occur (e.g., e7b23f0 'Add advisory triage tooling...', author Claude, 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5' + Claude-Session trailer, 2026 tooling commit), and the 2025-03 Sonatype expansion is likewise human-authored (Trevor Madge + Co-authored-by Matthieu Maitre, no AI markers). Missing-detection pattern therefore originates with the human denylist design at inception; NOT_AI stands on named-human authorship plus trailer-convention calibration, not merely absence of trailers.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Mechanism: PropertyUtilsBean performs unrestricted JavaBeans introspection; enum constants expose the java.lang.Enum#getDeclaringClass() getter as a 'declaringClass' bean property, and nested resolution reaches declaringClass.classLoader, giving unintended ClassLoader access from attacker-controlled property paths. BIC vs parent: fa9f99a (2003-03-03, Robert Burrell Donkin) created PropertyUtilsBean.java (1746 lines, CVS header 'v 1.1 2003/03/03') with unrestricted property resolution; parent 2634866 had no PropertyUtilsBean. However the static predecessor already existed: PropertyUtils.java is present in the repository's initial commit c44f209f (2001-03-27, Craig R. McClanahan) at src/share/, migrated to src/java/ by 7b7d9390 (2001-04-14), i.e. the same unrestricted static property-resolution model predates the 2003 BIC by ~2 years and the 2003 commit is a mechanical re-organization of it into a singleton (BIC diffstat: PropertyUtils.java -1442 lines, PropertyUtilsBean.java +1746). Runtime exposure boundary: the exposure is not new bytecode in fa9f99a but the combination of that model plus enum support (Java 5) plus BeanIntrospector plumbing added by 4e410e06 (2014-05-24, Oliver Heger, BEANUTILS-463), which created the extensible introspector list in PropertyUtilsBean; 1.9.2 (same BEANUTILS-463 line, 4e410e06 added SUPPRESS_CLASS for 'class' only) missed the sibling 'declaringClass'. Dual repair: 1.x fix 28ad955a (2025-05-25, Gary Gregory, pom 1.11.0-SNAPSHOT, changes.xml release 1.11.0) and 2.x fix bd20740d (2025-05-25, Gary Gregory, pom 2.0.0-M2-SNAPSHOT, changes.xml 2.x section) each add SuppressPropertiesBeanIntrospector.SUPPRESS_DECLARING_CLASS (suppressing 'declaringClass') and register it by default in PropertyUtilsBean resetBeanIntrospectors(); both fixes add EnumDeclaringClassTest proving the pre-fix exposure path 'fixture.testEnum.declaringClass.classLoader' resolves to a ClassLoader and that it throws NoSuchMethodException after the fix. AI evidence: no Co-Authored-By, Generated-by, or other AI trailers in any of the three commit bodies (BIC body has only a git-svn-id; both 2025 fix bodies are empty); BIC is CVS-era 2003 with author Robert Burrell Donkin (86 commits 2001-2004 in this repo) and the commit message explains a CVS-era architectural decision, so no positive AI evidence exists; verdict NOT_AI retained on the absence of positive AI markers plus pre-LLM human authorship, not inferred from marker absence alone. Version boundary: affected 1.x through 1.10.1 and 2.x through 2.0.0-M1 (any release carrying the unrestricted PropertyUtilsBean without SUPPRESS_DECLARING_CLASS); fixed in 1.11.0 and 2.0.0-M2.

round13_research.bug_semantics: OpenClaw owner/MCP authority inheritance across a trust boundary. In affected releases (<2026.5.20), a hook-triggered isolated-agent run (/hooks/agent with a valid hook token) could select the bundled CLI backend's loopback bearer token as the owner-scoped token (ownerToken) rather than the hook-appropriate non-owner token. The decision chain: (1) run.ts prepareCronRunContext set senderIsOwner = !isExternalHook where isExternalHook only recognizes content flagged with a hookExternalContentSource or a session whose key passes isExternalHookSession; (2) prepareCliRunContext set OPENCLAW_MCP_TOKEN to ownerToken when params.senderIsOwner === true; (3) the loopback MCP server authenticated by matching one of two per-session random tokens (mcp-http.ts:91-92, mcp-http.request.ts:126-128) and applied owner-only tool policy (applyOwnerOnlyToolPolicy) exposing cron/gateway/nodes owner-scoped tools to the caller of that token. Result: a caller holding only the hook token could drive owner-scoped MCP actions (advisory proof: persistent cron state), a privilege/authority escalation (CWE-266/284) and information exposure (CWE-200). The fix removed the entire sender-owner tool gating path, so configured tools stay visible for trusted sessions while command/channel-action auth still carries real sender identity.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Mechanism: SemanticsEnforcer.enforceTextSemantics handles text fields in two branches: a tags-gated branch runs sanitizeHtml with an allowlist when semantics.tags is set, and the else branch handles plain-text fields. Commit 5fd5c7b4bff58f6d3982bfd3ef2f948ed52cf540 ('fix(xss): remove overeager escaping of plain text (#17)', 2021-01-02, sr258; verified from its GitHub .patch) deleted the else-branch escape(unescape(newText)) call plus 19 lines of plain-text XSS tests, leaving plain-text field values in parentParams written to stored content with no HTML neutralization; attacker-controlled values in such fields persisted as stored XSS (CWE-79, GHSA-m7gm-v253-56hh, CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N). This removal landed on master through the squash 5f770a4bdfbac3d8b72bd31ca23340b9285a2d3c ('refactor(monorepo) (#1040)', 2021-02-16), whose patch body lists 'fix(xss): remove overeager escaping of plain text (#17)' and whose diff deletes 'newText = escape(unescape(newText));'; 5f770a4 is an ancestor of v9.0.0 and v9.3.2. BIC/parent comparison: parent 688a166da4dfe1f151515214084ccf644ea4881a is a renovate[bot] supertest bump with no text sanitization in src/SemanticsEnforcer.ts (show shows no text/escape/sanitize handling); BIC 8b7cca7783ab6e1d87c52383b6ea3a6b7d50f8b3 ('feat(security): xss protection in H5PEditor (#882)', 2020-11-04, sr258) first added enforceTextSemantics with the tags-gated sanitizeHtml block AND an else branch 'newText = escape(newText)' (verified in the BIC .patch hunk), so the exploitable no-else state was created later by the 2021 escape removal; the pre-sanitizer history is therefore parent (no handling) -> BIC (tags-gated sanitizeHtml + plain-text escape) -> 5fd5c7b4/5f770a4 (else sanitization removed; vulnerable state). Minimal fix: d001d164eff77c11e1d686fb66831e7475f8b872 ('fix(h5p-server): plain text strings are now sanitized (#3891)', 2025-01-23, sr258) adds exactly two lines, '} else { newText = sanitizeHtml(newText); }', closing the plain-text path with sanitize-html default filtering (blob 5ba17dac84->5b95d41a4d, verified in the .patch); it is an ancestor of origin/master. The identical two-line hunk also landed on the release branch via merge e94e6e09b2a94c343893368efca27fc0c485b7db (#3894, parent 4aa31e67b3014dec0ee3aca3af09fb87affbd1ab = v9.3.2, blob ad11235d4c->7d7ec5400e, one commit ahead of parent), which is an ancestor of v9.3.3; this resolves direct-member-vs-merge: d001d164 is the direct master landing and e94e6e0 is the changelog-cited release merge carrying the same fix. AI evidence: positive exclusion basis - every decisive commit (BIC, removal, monorepo squash, both fix landings) is authored by named human Sebastian Rettig <sr258@users.noreply.github.com>, the squash's only Co-authored-by is human JPSchellenberg <jps@Lumi.education>, AI-marker scans (copilot/claude/gpt/anthropic/openai/deepseek/gemini/llm/generated-with) returned zero hits on the BIC, removal, and fix patch artifacts, and the 2020-2021 commits predate widespread code-generation tools; no inference was drawn from marker absence alone. Version boundary: the vulnerable no-else state exists from v9.0.0 through v9.3.2 (v9.3.2 = 4aa31e67, file content via raw.githubusercontent.com confirms no else branch after the tags-gated block); v9.3.3 (tag 5730c0231dd77d70dcc0035d59b116eca930cd26, 2025-02-11) contains the fixed blob 7d7ec5400e with the else-sanitizeHtml branch; the GHSA page states affected < 9.3.3 and patched 9.3.3, published 2025-05-11. Verdict: NOT_AI.

BIC 0ba72477 (2026-01-08, feat: allow sessions_spawn cross-agent) first adds optional agentId/targetAgentId plus childSessionKey under the target agent, gated only by the requester's subagents.allowAgents list; a sandboxed session may then spawn an unsandboxed subagent under an allowed agent whose sandbox.mode=off, escaping the requester sandbox (no sandbox inheritance check). Verified true first-write: git log --follow on src/agents/tools/sessions-spawn-tool.ts shows the tool created 2026-01-06 (a279bcfeb) and the cross-agent branch appears first in this commit; parent d1ceb3aa always uses childSessionKey = agent:<requesterAgentId>:subagent:... with no agentId param (git show BIC^:...), so cross-agent downgrade was impossible before. BIC first shipped in v2026.1.8 (verified via git tag --contains; earlier v2026.1.x tags lack it). Fix b9aa2d43 (2026-03-02, fix(security): enforce sandbox inheritance for sessions_spawn, author Peter Steinberger) adds a check in spawnSubagentDirect (src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts) comparing requester vs child resolveSandboxRuntimeStatus and rejecting 'Sandboxed sessions cannot spawn unsandboxed subagents'; by then the tool path had been refactored onto spawnSubagentDirect (5a3a448bc4, 2026-02-16). Fix first ships in v2026.3.1 and is absent from v2026.2.26 (git merge-base --is-ancestor checks), matching affected <= 2026.2.26 / patched >= 2026.3.1. The OSV GIT event d76b224e is only an appcast docs commit, not the fix. causal_research.bug_semantics: BIC 52b69fb (2017-08-25, PR #1972 by Daniel Rampelt/drampelt) is the verified first-write (minimal introducing commit) of the ForwardAuth middleware. auth/forward.go Forward() builds the auth sub-request with forwardReq.Header = r.Header, copying the full client header set verbatim, so a client-supplied X-Forwarded-Prefix is forwarded untouched to the auth server. With trustForwardHeader=false, Traefik's writeHeader rebuilds X-Forwarded-* style headers (X-Forwarded-For/Proto/Port/Host/Uri/Method) but never X-Forwarded-Prefix, leaving an attacker-controlled prefix visible to the auth backend; this can bypass auth when Traefik sits behind a trusted upstream that would otherwise strip/rewrite those headers. Parent f16219f provably lacks any ForwardAuth code (no auth/forward.go, no Forward type), so 52b69fb is a true origin, not a rename. Fix 5e1de22 (2026-04-17, PR #12994 by Julien Salleyron/juliens) changes trustConfig trustForwardHeader to *bool: explicit false now deletes all X-Forwarded-* headers (DeleteXForwardedForHeaders including X-Forwarded-Prefix) before rebuilding the trusted set, while nil preserves legacy behavior. First fixed releases v2.11.43 / v3.6.14 / v3.7.0-rc.2 confirmed by both the official CVE record (CVE-2026-35051) and local git tag --contains of the fix. verdict NOT_AI: BIC is a 2017 pre-LLM human-authored feature commit with no AI markers; fix authored by a named human maintainer. NOT_AI is positively established, not merely inferred from an absent trailer.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Netty HTTP/1.0 request smuggling via TE+CL (CVE-2026-42581, GHSA-xxqh-mfjm-7mv9, CWE-444): HttpObjectDecoder strips a conflicting Content-Length when a message carries both Transfer-Encoding: chunked and Content-Length, but ONLY when treating the message as HTTP/1.1 - for HTTP/1.0 the guard is false, so Netty decodes the body as chunked while leaving Content-Length intact on the forwarded HttpMessage; a downstream CL-first proxy can disagree on message boundaries (request smuggling). Verified in local clone netty__netty: BIC 8494b046ec7e4f28dbd44bc699cc4c4c92251729 (2019-12-13, Norman Maurer, 'Verify we do not receive multiple content-length headers or ... when using HTTP/1.1 (#9865)', parent 9a0ccf24) is the FIRST write of this HTTP/1.1-gated TE+CL handling - the parent has no TE+CL coexistence handling at all (bare chunked -> READ_CHUNK_SIZE), so the HTTP/1.1-only gate that HTTP/1.0 bypasses originates here (this resolves the two-reviewer split: George selected this first-write; Michael selected the later 62903462 throw-to-strip change (#10003, 2020-02-10) which only reshaped the existing gate). Direct fix 84530fa (4.2/main, 2026-05-04, Chris Vest, private fork merge, parent e62d403f) and 4.1 backport d2475645 (parent 6eea1bc7 still vulnerable) reject Transfer-Encoding on non-HTTP/1.1 under RFC 9112 and harden TE+CL. Tag ancestry verified: netty-4.1.132.Final and netty-4.2.0 (contain BIC, no fix); first fixed tags netty-4.1.133.Final (d2475645) and netty-4.2.13.Final (84530fa) match advisory. AI: BIC is 2019 named-human maintainer work with no AI markers; fixes by Chris Vest, Co-authored-by Adwait Kumar Singh (remediation only). NOT_AI supported.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Mechanism: picklescan fails to flag pickle REDUCE globals targeting lib2to3.pgen2.pgen.ParserGenerator.make_label; entry absent from the scanner blocklist, so malicious pickles pass as safe while pickle.load() reaches the gadget (CVE-2025-71343, GHSA-p9w7-82w4-7q8m, fixed in commit 1931c2d0 which explicitly lists this GHSA and adds "lib2to3.pgen2.pgen": {"ParserGenerator.make_label"}). Verified lineage: BIC is c1d5abdc 'Implement Pickle scanner' (2022-09-04, Matthieu Maitre) whose tree first writes src/picklescan/scanner.py; parent 6a76b8c3 has no src/ at all (boilerplate-only tree), so the miss originates at scanner inception. BIC blob (44974c08) contains no lib2to3 reference whatsoever and its _suspicious_globals list is minimal (~9 entries); git log -S 'lib2to3' over scanner.py shows lib2to3 entries first appear only on 2025-08-26 (aecd11be adds Grammar.loads, then 1931c2d0 adds ParserGenerator.make_label). Gadget availability/omission timing: lib2to3.pgen2.pgen.ParserGenerator is CPython stdlib present decades before 2022 (lib2to3 shipped Python 2.6 through 3.12), so the omission was a completeness gap in the initial blocklist, not a gadget that postdated scanner inception; aecd11be (a sibling-GHSA add of Grammar.loads hours earlier, also Matthieu) does not pre-introduce this miss. Fix boundary: 1931c2d0 (2025-08-26, Matthieu Maitre, subject 'Missing detection when calling Python functions (#49)', no AI trailer; Co-authored-by Matthieu Maitre <mmaitre@microsoft.com> is the same human under a second email); tag v0.0.29 points to aecd11be without the fix and v0.0.30 points to 1931c2d0, matching CVE affected <0.0.30 / unaffected 0.0.30. causal_research.bug_semantics: Persisted XSS (CWE-79) in timesheet descriptions. Verified in local canonical clone kimai/kimai (remote https://github.com/kimai/kimai.git; kevinpapst/kimai2 is the pre-rename alias of the same history). BIC 4c277fe1 (2018-09-02, PR #296, allow markdown in timesheet descriptions) introduced the Twig filter desc2html (timesheetContent, is_safe html) routing the description through Markdown::toHtml($content, false), i.e. Parsedown 1.x setSafeMode(false); with kimai.timesheet.markdown enabled, the user timesheet template switched from entry.description|nl2br to unescaped entry.description|desc2html, so HTML/SVG in a description renders as trusted markup for anyone viewing timesheet/export/invoice. Parent 9f6079ad (2018-09-02, added option to delete invoice template, #294) renders the same field as entry.description|nl2br in templates/timesheet/index.html.twig (auto-escaped) and plain entry.description in templates/admin/timesheet.html.twig, with no desc2html filter anywhere (checked src/Twig/MarkdownExtension.php, config/services.yaml and both templates). git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms 9f6079ad is the immediate parent of 4c277fe1. Minimum fix a0e8aa3a (2019-07-14, PR #962, fixed xss in timesheet description) adds the Twig |escape filter before desc2html at every remaining desc2html call site (templates/timesheet/index.html.twig, templates/timesheet/export.html.twig, templates/timesheet-team/export.html.twig, templates/invoice/index.html.twig, templates/export/renderer/default.html.twig, templates/export/renderer/pdf.html.twig); the former admin/timesheet.html.twig call site had already been removed, so the fix covers all remaining vulnerable call sites. The same commit also flips markdownToHtml true-to-false (toHtml($content, false)); md2html has no remaining template callers at the fix commit, so this is an orthogonal default flip, not the description-XSS control and not enabling Parsedown safe mode for descriptions. AI exclusion positive evidence: raw commit messages of BIC 4c277fe1 and fix a0e8aa3a (git cat-file / od -c) contain only the subject line and blank padding, no trailers at all, no Co-Authored-by, no Generated-by/Co-authored-by AI markers, no AI tool syntax; author and committer identity Kevin Papst kevinpapst@users.noreply.github.com (committer field GitHub noreply@github.com via GitHub web-flow merge), both commits dated 2018/2019. Version boundaries from git tag --contains: BIC first shipped in 0.5 (through 1.0.x), fix first shipped in 1.1; affected < 1.1, fixed >= 1.1.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Mechanism: the LFS upload API builds the blob-store path from the client-controlled oid query parameter with no validation or sanitization. Commit 0a573a56 added app/api/controller/lfs/upload.go whose Upload() handler does objPath = getLFSObjectPath(pointer.OId) and passes it straight to blobStore.Upload; getLFSObjectPath (app/api/controller/lfs/controller.go) is fmt.Sprintf(lfsObjectsPathFormat, oid) with lfsObjectsPathFormat = 'lfs/%s' (controller.go:35). The route (app/router/git.go, GitLFSHandler) binds PUT /info/lfs-objects to HandleLFSUpload, which reads the oid via request.GetObjectIDFromQuery -> QueryParamOrError with no format or path checks; the controller also only checks repo push permission (getRepoCheckAccess), so any authenticated user with push access can supply an oid containing ../ to escape the lfs/ prefix and write arbitrary files via blobStore.Upload (arbitrary file write, CWE-22/CWE-73, CVSS 8.8 PR:L). BIC/parent comparison: immediate parent 6da9821b lacks app/api/controller/lfs/upload.go entirely; the BIC added upload.go plus the LFS controller/handler/router/store wiring, including the unvalidated path construction, so the BIC is the original introduction. History checks: no lfs-related files exist in the parent lineage; git log -S getLFSObjectPath over 6da9821b..21c5ce42 shows no intermediate introduction or change; and v3.2.0 tag (2025-05-22) contains the BIC, proving the defect shipped in a public release before the 3.3.0 fix. Minimal fix: commit 21c5ce42 (2025-08-08, PR #4235 per subject, squash) touches only app/api/controller/lfs/upload.go and (a) rejects upload when lfsStore.Find shows the OID already exists, (b) hashes the limited upload body with SHA-256 and requires hex(sha256(content)) == strings.TrimPrefix(pointer.OId, 'sha256:') before calling getLFSObjectPath, and (c) improves a duplicate error message; since any successful upload now requires the OID to equal the content hash, the path component is confined to hex characters and traversal/absolute-path injection is closed; this is the only change to the vulnerable function, so it is the minimum repair. AI evidence: no AI markers in the BIC commit message, full BIC diff, or fix diff (grep for Copilot/Claude/Anthropic/Cursor/Gemini/ChatGPT/OpenAI/co-authored/ai-generated all negative); the BIC tree contains no AI assistant config files (the only 'AI' file hits are the Harness product feature web/src/ar/components/AISearchInput/). The BIC is a single-parent squash/merge of a feature branch whose message is review-note prose and unrelated PR-subject pickups, with no tool trailers; the merge-baseline diff for upload.go is identical to the full commit diff, so organization merge infrastructure does not change the causal authorship account. Author identity: author and committer Atefeh Mohseni Ejiyeh <atefeh.mohseni-ejiyeh@harness.io> with Harness org domain on both BIC and fix. Missing-marker absence is not proof of human authorship and is not used as such; the positive human-attribution evidence is the consistent named Harness engineer identity plus absence of any positive AI marker in the causal diff. Independent sources: GitHub advisory GHSA-w469-hj2f-jpr5 page ('Arbitrary File Write in Gitness LFS server', fix = commit 21c5ce42, patch = 3.3.0) and the official CVE.org CVE-2025-58158 record (CNA GitHub_M, CWE-22/CWE-73, affected < 3.3.0, patch 3.3.0, same fix SHA) both match the local-git mechanism, authorship, and fix evidence. Version boundary: affected < 3.3.0 (v3.2.0 public tag already carries the vulnerable code; v3.1.x predates the LFS feature); fixed in 3.3.0, which contains the fix commit per local tag ancestry.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Mechanism: Config._valid splits a string config value with an alternation regex that exhibits catastrophic backtracking on inputs like 100k word-chars followed by an equals sign or a quote (CWE-1333). TRUE BIC: commit 0c31dede (2014-11-24, Tjatse) created lib/tools/Config.js containing the first string-to-array split in Config._valid - a value.split() with an alternation of a key-equals-quoted-value branch, a bare quoted-run branch, and whitespace; see the BIC diff for the literal pattern. The supplied BIC 70539217 (2014-11-26) is a refinement of that regex, not the origin: its parent 3143ed21 already contains the 0c31dede pattern, and empirical timing on the fix's own PoC inputs shows the predecessor regex is already catastrophic (about 1.7s at 50k chars, 7.1s at 100k), while the 70539217 replacement is equally catastrophic (4.7s at 50k, 18.8s at 100k) - the BIC/parent pair differs in matched-text detail, not in resource behavior. Minimum fix 8b935480 (2026-04-28, Unitech, v7.0.0) replaces the single value.split() alternation with a value.match() based tokenizer using per-branch bounded patterns plus quote-stripping, preserving prior token semantics (quoted segments captured and unquoted, whitespace-split plain tokens); the catastrophic unbounded branches are gone, and the fix adds test/programmatic/issue_6075_redos.mocha.js using 100k-char adversarial inputs. AI evidence: no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with/Copilot/Cursor/Claude/GPT/OpenAI/Anthropic markers on 0c31dede, 70539217, or 8b935480 (positive-absence only); all are 2014/2026 commits by human-identified authors (Tjatse personal Gmail, Unitech corporate Keymetrics). Version boundary: the defective split path first shipped in pm2 0.12.2 (first tag containing 0c31dede; 0c31dede is 55 commits after 0.12.1 and 70539217 is 83 commits after 0.12.1); fixed in 7.0.0. Independent sources: NVD CVE-2025-5891 (CNA vuldb, CWE-1333, affected up to 6.0.6, PoC public) and GHSA-x5gf-qvw8-r2rm (SEMVER introduced 0, fixed 7.0.0, references fix commit 8b935480); OSV's GIT-range introduced commit e8855398 (pm2@6.0.5) and last_affected e71120a5 (6.0.6) are advisory reporting events, not code lineage - 0c31dede is an ancestor of both, consistent with code-first, advisory-later.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Mechanism: DefaultSmtpRequest stores caller-supplied CharSequence parameters without any CR/LF filtering, so a CRLF embedded in a parameter injects an attacker-controlled SMTP command into the wire stream (SMTP command injection / email-auth bypass). BIC: 562d8d220028fbb3d62028bc5879a121dff2fdbd, 'Add smtp codec (client side only)'. Parent-vs-BIC diff: the parent 24254b159f3df12ce6b3c99b2f90dc8d27f8f234 tree contains no codec-smtp module (ls-tree of codec-smtp is empty at parent); the BIC adds the whole codec-smtp module including DefaultSmtpRequest.java whose two parameterized constructors pass parameters straight to SmtpUtils.toUnmodifiableList / Collections.unmodifiableList with no validation. git log --follow between BIC and the 2025 fix parent e4632f547bef22ba9f2237d53f84628f8e3b4630 shows only two unrelated commits for this file (nohttp check, unstable annotation), so the BIC is the origin of the vulnerable constructor code. Minimum fix: merge 1782e8c2060a244c4d4e6f9d9112d5517ca05120 (4.2) and its 4.1 cherry-pick 2b3fddd3339cde1601f622b9ce5e54c39f24c3f9 each add exactly one guard line per vulnerable constructor, SmtpUtils.validateSMTPParameters(parameters), plus new SmtpUtils.validateSMTPParameter throwing IllegalArgumentException on any parameter containing a carriage return or line feed, plus regression tests. Version boundaries from local tags: the 4.2 fix merge is contained in netty-4.2.7.Final, 4.2.8.Final and 4.2.9.Final tags but not 4.2.6; the 4.1 fix 2b3fddd3 is contained in netty-4.1.128.Final and later but not 4.1.127; the GHSA fixed versions 4.1.129/4.2.8 are conservative advisory bounds while OSV's 4.1.128/4.2.7 are the actual first-fix tags. First vulnerable release containing the BIC is the 4.1.0 line (first tag netty-4.1.0.CR7). Date reconciliation: the single BIC commit has author date 2015-09-04T14:27:18+02:00 and committer date 2016-04-07T18:42:17+02:00; both supplied reports quoted the same commit but each picked one timestamp, and the file header copyright 2016 plus the tag scan confirm the code shipped in the 4.1.0 line released 2016. AI disposition: positive AI evidence exists only on the fix/report side - the fix commit is authored by DepthFirst Disclosures and their public blog states an AI agent discovered the vulnerability; that is discovery evidence and is not introducing authorship. The BIC commit message and git notes contain no AI markers (no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Claude, Copilot or similar) and the author is a named Netty maintainer; per protocol marker absence is not treated as positive exclusion, but the only AI-positive evidence concerns 2025 discovery, so the BIC remains NOT_AI on the available decisive evidence while discovery credit stays with the AI agent.

LINEAGE (independently verified in local clone mmaitre314__picklescan): initial scanner c1d5abdcc7 (2022-09-04, Matthieu Maitre) handled STACK_GLOBAL with fixed ops[n-2]/ops[n-1] SHORT_BINUNICODE reads only. BIC 18c978e9 (2022-09-05, single parent 9c31e179 confirmed via rev-list) rewrote _list_globals for multiple-pickle support and first wrote the range(1,n) walker; the diff minus-side and 9c31e179:scanner.py show the parent has no range loop (fixed-index form only), and c1d5abd is an ancestor of 9c31e179, so the off-by-one bound originates in this BIC, not in the initial scanner. Between 2022 and 2025 the walker body grew opcode-family support (MEMOIZE/PUT/GET resolution, UNICODE/BINUNICODE/BINUNICODE8 string handling) through later named-human commits (Matthieu Maitre, Luc Georges, quasar098; e.g. e99f3ae PUT support, aeb7641 memoized values, 40001cd INST); this secondary history is preserved separately and the CVE boundary stays the range(1,n) bound first written in the BIC. FIX: 58983e1c (PR #46, 2025-08-09, authored by Matthieu Maitre, GitHub-committer squash; only commit in local history changing the loop text per -S search) changes the bound to range(1, n+1) and adds STRING/BINSTRING/SHORT_BINSTRING to the recognized string family, closing the index-0 blind spot; tag v0.0.27 == 58983e1c and v0.0.26 == 2a8383cf (the OSV-listed alternate commit, a README/setup.cfg image-link change, still vulnerable), so first fixed release boundary is 0.0.27. Calibrated across the full repo history, AI-authored work is explicit in git metadata (commits authored by Claude first appear 2026-08-23, e.g. 76dd85d/e7b23f0, with Claude-Session trailers), while 2022-2025 scanner commits carry named human authors only; absence-of-trailer alone is therefore not relied on. round13_research.bug_semantics: Zalo zalouser personal-channel monitor accepts non-numeric allowFrom/groupAllowFrom entries and, at startup, binds them to whatever friend currently has that displayName (or group has that name). Because display names are mutable by users, an attacker can rename their account to an allowlisted name and so be resolved into the numeric allowlist, passing isSenderAllowed admission for impersonation/spoofing (CWE-290).
evidence: CVE-2026-53857 / GHSA-8c59-hr4w-qg69: Zalo allowFrom could bind to mutable display names, CWE-290, CVSS 8.1.

Source-to-sink chain: allowFrom/groupAllowFrom raw name -> startup name-to-ID binding -> isSenderAllowed senderId admission -> agent processes message.

Zalo zalouser personal channel resolves non-numeric allowFrom / groupAllowFrom config entries to friend/group IDs by matching mutable displayName at startup, then merges the matched numeric IDs into the allowlist (extensions/zalouser/src/monitor.ts monitorZalouserProvider startup block).

An attacker who can change their Zalo display name to an allowlisted name captures that allowlist slot, spoofing an allowed sender (CWE-290, self-descriptive vulnerability).

round13_research.bug_semantics: OpenClaw host environment sanitizer used an incomplete denylist for Node.js runtime control variables: workspace .env values, tool env overrides and skill env blocks could pass NODE_REDIRECT_WARNINGS, NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE, NODE_REPL_HISTORY and NODE_V8_COVERAGE through the shared sanitizer (CWE-184). A lower-trust env source could thereby influence a later Node child process startup or coverage output path when the process was launched under the accepted environment.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Command injection in Deno node:child_process with shell:true bypassing CVE-2026-27190 (GHSA-4c96-w8v2-p28j): PR #31999 added escapeShellArg which wraps args in POSIX single quotes, but transformDenoShellCommand re-quoted args containing shell variable references ($VAR) in DOUBLE quotes to preserve expansion - double quotes do not suppress backtick substitution in POSIX sh, so an arg mixing $VAR with backticks/$(...) regains command injection. Verified in local clone denoland__deno: BIC 9132ad95 (2026-02-02 10:17 -0300, Felipe Cardozo, subject fix(ext/node): escape more shell args (#31999), single parent b51441cc, follow-up to #31838) - patch shows escapeShellArg added (single quotes + embedded-quote escaping on POSIX, double quotes on Windows) and the command built as [escapeShellArg(file), ...args.map(escapeShellArg)] which then flows into transformDenoShellCommand whose $VAR branch re-quotes with double quotes; parent lacks escapeShellArg. Direct fix b4d4a5bc (2026-03-02 10:34 +0100, same author, subject fix:(ext/node): escape simple quotes in node:child_process (#32336), parent 9c81a230) restricts the double-quote re-quoting: only args free of backticks/$(/backslash get double quotes, otherwise single quotes with proper escaping - regression tests include a backtick+$VAR payload and a double-quote breakout case. Release boundary via local tags: v2.7.0/v2.7.1 contain BIC without fix (2.7.1 merge-base confirmed), v2.7.2 contains the fix - matching advisory affected v2.7.0/v2.7.1 fixed 2.7.2. causal_research.bug_semantics: Mechanism: phpseclib/File/ASN1.php BER-decodes OBJECT_IDENTIFIER content with an unbounded septet loop, so an oversized OID in a certificate drives quadratic string/BigInteger work and memory growth in decodeBER (CWE-400 DoS). BIC resolution: local clone of phpseclib/phpseclib shows the 2019 candidate e7934615 ('ASN1: revamp how OIDs are handled', 2019-04-30, terrafrost) only refactors existing code - its parent 756b2474 already contains File/ASN1.php with the identical unbounded septet loop (removed lines 'while ($content_pos < $content_len)' over OID content), and the refactor's new _decodeOID() keeps the same unbounded 'while ($pos < $len)' loop with no cap. The 2012 candidate 441ada05 ('add an X.509 encoder / decoder', 2012-03-11, Jim Wigginton <terrafrost@php.net>) is the first introduction: its parent 228fb3ce contains no phpseclib/File/ASN1.php (git ls-tree shows only 15 crypto/math/net files, no ASN.1 or OID decoding anywhere), and the commit adds File/ASN1.php (1043 lines) including the unbounded OID septet loop at _decode_ber. The vulnerable construct originates at 441ada05, so the BIC conflict resolves in favor of the 2012 commit; the 2019 commit is a refactor that preserved the flaw. Minimal fix: e3253100 ('ASN1: limit OID length', 2024-02-24, terrafrost <terrafrost@gmail.com>) adds exactly 'if ($len > 4096) { return false; }' at the top of _decodeOID() (OpenJDK ObjectIdentifier limit referenced in comment) plus a mal-cert-02.der unit test asserting decodeBER returns false; no other behavioral change. Version boundary: git tag --contains confirms e3253100 first appears in 1.0.23, 2.0.47, and 3.0.36 (released 2024-02-25); 1.0.22/2.0.46/3.0.35 lack the 4096 check and ASN1.php at 1.0.22 has no limit, so affected range is 2012-03-11 (441ada05) through before 1.0.23/2.0.47/3.0.36. Fernando's release attribution (1.0.23/2.0.47/3.0.36, terrafrost fix, OSV fixed SHAs being later merges) is preserved and confirmed; release tips are tags, not the direct patch. causal_research.bug_semantics: Module/advisory: picklescan failed to flag a pickle REDUCE payload calling asyncio.unix_events._UnixSubprocessTransport._start (GHSA-q77w-mwjj-7mqx). Mechanism: from scanner inception the deny-list (_suspicious_globals/_unsafe_globals) is looked up by exact g.module with value '*' or a name set, so a global whose module string is the submodule 'asyncio.unix_events' never matched any entry and was never dangerous-flagged (inception build did not even warn on unlisted modules). Verified lineage: BIC c1d5abd (Implement Pickle scanner, 2022-09-04) is the first write of src/picklescan/scanner.py and of the deny-list/exact-module lookup (git show --name-status: scanner.py is A; GLOBAL/STACK_GLOBAL parsing and exact _suspicious_globals.get(g[0]) matching exist in this commit); parent 6a76b8c (2022-09-03) contains only boilerplate (.gitignore, LICENSE, README.md, conda.yaml, requirements.txt, setup.cfg) with no scanner code, so no vulnerable detection existed in the parent and the BIC is the minimal inception of the omission. git log -S asyncio over src/picklescan/scanner.py returns exactly b1d7c63 (add 'asyncio': '*', 2024-09-25, PR #30 by Luc Georges), 1931c2d (fix), 28a7b4e (generalization); no pre-fix revision ever contained an asyncio.unix_events entry or submodule-prefix matching, so the archive-candidate BIC b1d7c638 is only a later deny-list expansion whose exact-module '*' semantics (unchanged since inception, verified in scanner.py at b1d7c638: unsafe_filter = _unsafe_globals.get(g.module)) never covered submodule-addressed globals - it neither introduced nor worsened the gap, and its parent 15c0dbd3 likewise has no asyncio entry. Fix: 1931c2d (Missing detection when calling Python functions (#49), 2025-08-26, Matthieu Maitre) is a 10-GHSA multi-advisory commit; the direct per-module repair for this advisory is the added entry 'asyncio.unix_events': {'_UnixSubprocessTransport._start'}. Release boundary: v0.0.29..v0.0.30 contains exactly 1931c2d and git tag --contains 1931c2d starts at v0.0.30, so first fixed release is v0.0.30 and all earlier releases (scanner inception v0.0.1..v0.0.29) are affected (<0.0.30 per advisory). Follow-up 28a7b4e (v0.0.31) generalizes the fix (top-level '*' deny entries propagate to submodules) and removes the explicit entry, preserving coverage. AI role: none on the BIC, established by positive evidence: BIC is by Matthieu Maitre, repository creator who alone authored the first three commits (2022-09-03/04), years before AI tooling appears; the author census across the whole history is named humans plus one dependabot[bot] commit, with zero Claude/Copilot-style co-author trailers in commit messages; the fix commit shows only the maintainer's own dual-email trailer (mmaitre@live.com + Co-authored-by mmaitre@microsoft.com). Verdict NOT_AI confirmed for the BIC.

causal_research.bug_semantics: NOT_AI. Defect is unbounded Miller-Rabin in Math_BigInteger::isPrime()/randomPrime() (CWE-400): a malformed cert supplying an extremely large prime makes isPrime() burn CPU. 3.x BIC is 6298d1cd (terrafrost, 2023-03-02, 'PrimeField: prevent infinite loop with composite primefields'), the CVE-2023-27560 remediation that first uncommented/enabled the live 'if (!$modulo->isPrime())' guard in Math/PrimeField::__construct; git blame on 3.0.35 (PrimeField.php L47) resolves to 6298d1cd, and its immediate parent 3b6030d8 still has the check commented out. That is the first live reachability of unbounded isPrime() on attacker-controlled cert moduli. The 1.x/2.x origin is distinct and now resolved: there is no PrimeField in 1.0/2.0; the unbounded isPrime() and randomPrime() public methods were introduced together in 839ea8c1 (Jim Wigginton, 2009-11-03), and in 1.0/2.0 isPrime() is only internally reachable via Crypt/RSA private-key generation -> randomPrime() (bounded by the requested key size); there is no cert-reading sink (git grep shows no isPrime/randomPrime caller outside Math/BigInteger.php and Crypt/RSA.php in 1.0/2.0). The 1.x/2.x exposure is the unbounded public API, matching GHSA-2528-jw5q-ww88 impact ('anyone ... testing the primality of a number'); OSV records 1.x as introduced 0.1.1. Fix ad5dbdf2 (terrafrost, 2024-02-23, 'BigInteger: put guardrails on isPrime() and randomPrime()') adds an 8196-bit guardrail to isPrime()/randomPrime(), forward-merged to 2.0 (2870c8fa) and 3.0 (0358eb163, 'Merge branch 2.0 into 3.0'), with follow-up c55b7519 fixing a getLength() typo. Every causal object is human-authored (6298d1cd/ad5dbdf2 by terrafrost, 839ea8c1 by Jim Wigginton) with no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with/bot trailer; 839ea8c1 predates LLM coding assistants. round13_research.bug_semantics: Discord (and Slack) message read actions accepted an arbitrary caller-supplied channelId and called rest.get(Routes.channelMessages(channelId)) with no channel allowlist / policy check. The only gate was isActionEnabled('messages'), which checks whether the messages action category is enabled at all — not which channels may be read. A low-privilege caller (peer/agent with enabled messages) could read messages from any channel/guild the bot's token can see, skipping the guild channel allowlist that inbound monitor.ts enforces (Blocked discord channel ... not in guild channel allowlist). This is CWE-862 Missing Authorization: read action bypass of the established channel allowlist.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CVE-2026-34166 (GHSA-mmg9-6m6j-jqqx) is a memory-limit undercharging bug in the liquidjs replace filter. BIC=e443068c (2024-07-09, feat DoS prevention #250) first wired memoryLimit.use() into src/filters/string.ts replace(), charging only str.length (input) while still executing str.split(pattern).join(replacement) whose output can be str.length + (parts.length-1)*(replacement.length-pattern.length); the split/join amplification bypasses the opt-in memoryLimit guard. BIC 73e9e787 (2026-01-19, 'feat: unify device auth + pairing', author+committer Peter Steinberger) is the verified first write of that construct: it added the role/scopes/deviceIdentity connect fields to src/gateway/call.ts and src/gateway/client.ts (scopes default ['operator.admin']) and introduced server-side authorizeGatewayMethod; parent 47d1f23d has no scopes/role or method-authorization code in call.ts, client.ts, or server-methods.ts (verified by file inspection), while cron-tool.ts and gateway-tool.ts already existed. Exploitability matured in the same design series: 9dbc1435 (2026-01-20) added operator.read/write scope enforcement (scoped-token deployments), and the owner-only-tool concept started 2026-02-04 in 392bbddf29c (PR #9202, Gustavo Madeira Santana/Victor Mier) listing only whatsapp_login; cron/gateway were never owner-gated until the fix. causal_research.bug_semantics: Mechanism: POST /$/datasets builds a Fuseki service/dataset config from request data (assemblerFromForm / assemblerFromUpload multipart / assemblerFromBody) and writes it into the server configuration area, so a client can define arbitrary dataset assemblers including file-backed TDB locations; parameter validation and upload gating were absent. BIC 9c9d5b8727f46c6b6b3eae8f93a4f13d6bf2622b (Promote Fuseki2 to trunk, 2014-09-19, git-svn-id r1626183, author=committer Andy Seaborne <andy@apache.org>) is a 316-file, ~59.6k-line import that first adds jena-fuseki2 to trunk; its sole parent 4cf523b4f49646e51905a3d5e0a5e1c59f24eb42 (Suppress deprecation warnings, 2014-09-18, Andy Seaborne, 1 file jena-arq/src/main/java/com/hp/hpl/jena/query/Query.java +1 line) contains no jena-fuseki2 directory and no ActionDatasets.java, so git --follow for jena-fuseki2/.../mgt/ActionDatasets.java terminates exactly at the promotion commit; the immediate-parent diff 4cf523b4..9c9d5b87 is the whole Fuseki2 import. Pre-promotion upstream origin: no pre-promotion git history or git notes for the Fuseki2 module exists in the local clone (searched all branches, tags and notes; the module never existed in jena-fuseki1 mgt code at the parent — its mgt servlets lack any config-file dataset-creation path, and its only upload code is GSP/SPARQL_Upload data upload). The vulnerable state (unvalidated body/multipart config parsing, no allowConfigFiles gate, no path validation) is present verbatim at the 2014 import and at jena-2.12.1 (first release tag containing jena-fuseki2; jena-2.12.0 tag 2014-07-26 predates the import and does not contain it), so the trunk promotion commit is the effective first-write of the vulnerable code path into release history. Minimal fix: 35350569b4c1fd432d92e7c92af9597c4400debe (GH-3288, authored 2025-06-13, committed 2025-07-02, Andy Seaborne <andy@apache.org>; parent e65489642ac3402ef23e7a3c4361d47a489213a4) disables multipart config upload outright, gates body-config behind the new default-off system property fuseki:allowAddByConfigFile (FusekiAdmin.allowConfigFiles returns false unless the property equals true), adds service-name path validation (isValidServiceName rejects embedded slashes and /.. traversal) and TDB location validation (isValidTDBLocation rejects .. components), rejects a missing service name, and consumes unread request bodies; companion commit 03c5265910aa3a27907bf54f6b4aaae3409afa4f applies identical validation to the jena-fuseki-webapp copy of ActionDatasets. The fix landed on main 2025-06-13 and is contained in release tag jena-5.5.0 (2025-07-14); tag jena-5.4.0 (2025-04-14) still contains the vulnerable unvalidated assemblerFromBody/multipart path. AI attribution: no AI marker evidence found on BIC 9c9d5b87 (2014, pre-dates the code-assistant era; single author Andy Seaborne who is also the sole committer; commit message is a plain SVN promotion message; ~59.6k lines over 316 files is a bulk import of an existing module, not generated-style code; file layout and Java style match contemporary hand-written Fuseki/Jena code, and every mgt file under jena-fuseki2 is coherently cross-referenced with the rest of the module). This is positive human-authorship evidence (git-svn promotion of operator-authored work by the module maintainer), not merely an absence of markers, so the source verdict NOT_AI is independently supported for the BIC. causal_research.bug_semantics: Mechanism: NimbusJwtDecoder.withIssuerLocation / NimbusReactiveJwtDecoder.withIssuerLocation only derived a JWK-set builder (fetch discovery config, validate provider-configuration issuer against metadata, default algorithms), with an empty Nimbus claims verifier and no issuer-claim validator attached to the built decoder; build() therefore accepted any JWT signed by a key in the issuer's discovered JWK set with a missing or different iss claim (issuer trust confusion). Lineage (verified in local git): BIC 76eba9bd (2023-04-12, author/committer Josh Cummings, message 'Add withIssuerLocation / Closes gh-10309') is the true first write of both APIs; parent 9ee8202 has zero withIssuerLocation occurrences repo-wide, and diff shows both method families introduced with A/M file states plus JwkSetUriJwtDecoderBuilder refactor. Same commit rewrote JwtDecoders.fromIssuerLocation to compose the new builder and then explicitly decoder.setJwtValidator(JwtValidators.createDefaultWithIssuer(issuer)), demonstrating issuer-bound validation was known-required on that path but was omitted inside the new public builder API the advisory covers. Fix: 68b820ed (2026-04-15, 'Check Issuer with Issuer Provided', Josh Cummings, single parent 44d32815, atomic 4-file/62-insertion change) adds .validator(JwtValidators.createDefaultWithIssuer(issuer)) on the withIssuerLocation factories, defaults builder validator to JwtValidators.createDefault(), and applies decoder.setJwtValidator(this.validator) in build(). Release boundary: first OSS tags containing the fix are 6.5.10 (2026-04-20) and 7.0.5; 6.5.9 and 7.0.4 verified NOT to contain 68b820ed. BIC first shipped in 6.1.0-RC1/6.1.0, so the flaw exists from API introduction (6.1.0) through 6.5.9/7.0.4. AI evidence (positive): named human maintainer Josh Cummings authored and committed the BIC in April 2023 for human feature request gh-10309 ('Add NimbusJwtDecoder#withIssuerLocation'); commit has no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with/bot trailer; repo calibration over 2022-11..2023-08 (1255 commits) shows zero AI contribution trailers (only human GitHub co-author entries), while 2025-2026 commits do carry AI trailers (e.g. two Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6), so absence of a trailer is meaningful against a calibrated convention. Supplied NOT_AI verdict confirmed.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Free5GC UDM null-byte injection in the supi path parameter of the Nudm_SubscriberDataManagement API (GHSA-p9hg-pq3q-v9gv / CVE-2026-33191, CWE-158 + CWE-248). Mechanism: HandleGetAmData (internal/sbi/api_subscriberdatamanagement.go) copies the raw supi from the gin path (c.Params.ByName('supi')) with no validation, passes it to GetAmDataProcedure, which sets queryAmDataRequest.UeId=&supi and builds the UDR client via CreateUDMClientToUDR(supi) -> getUdrURI(); the supi (containing URL-encoded %00 bytes) is embedded in the UDR URI path e.g. /nudr-dr/v2/subscription-data/<supi>/... and Go net/url rejects the control character ('invalid control character in URL'), so the request errors out as 500 Internal Server Error instead of 400, enabling remote denial of service (advisory: Automatable=yes, VA:H). Root cause is the absence of input validation on the supi/supiOrSuci identifier from the very first commit: BIC 371e495 is the repository ROOT commit (no parents) by free5gc-org (2020-04-28), OpenGPT/OpenAPI Generator scaffold (source file header 'Generated by: OpenAPI Generator'), where GetAmData (then in SubscriberDataManagement/api_access_and_mobility_subscription_data_retrieval.go) already copied supi from the path unchecked. The 2024-05-13 refactor 2d42b1a8 only added a 12-line router stub for internal/subsystem restructuring; it did not introduce or validate the handler, and follow-on commits (e.g. 84bf661 openapi re-regen) preserved the unchecked copy. Fix parent 9308405 (pre-fix HEAD, inside v1.4.1) still carries the unchecked getter, confirming the flaw predates and spans the entire release line. Fix: 1e47510 'fix: add validation in Sdm' by wiwi <a31625802@gmail.com> (2026-01-19), merged via PR #79 merge 88de9fa (Feng Tu 2026-01-20); v1.4.2 is the first tag containing the fix (advisory: affected < 1.4.2). The fix adds boundary validation validator.IsValidSupi/IsValidGpsi in HandleGetAmData, HandleUnsubscribe, HandleModify, HandleGetIdTranslationResult, returning 400 with cause MANDATORY_IE_INCORRECT instead of forwarding unvalidated identifiers to UDR. causal_research.bug_semantics: Cross-tenant payroll disclosure and creation in prospero-flow-crm (CVE-2026-19870): PayrollIndexController listed payroll with no company scope and PayrollRequest validated user_id with unscoped exists:user,id, so an authenticated payroll user could read other tenants' payroll records and create payroll records attributed to other companies' employees. Two origins, resolved from rewritten-history confusion (the archive's f36c2a1 'root/squash' claim is wrong - f36c2a1 is the unrelated CVE-2026-19734 product fix): (1) DISCLOSURE origin 5804831d (2024-02-12 00:47 +0100, Gustavo Novaro, 'New Payroll module...', parent 18742f57) first adds app/Http/Controllers/Payroll/PayrollIndexController.php + app/Models/Payroll.php with getAllByYear() implemented as unscoped Payroll::whereYear('payment_date', $year)->get() (raw file verified at that SHA) - the cross-tenant listing exposure begins with the module's first write; (2) CREATION origin 04d1afd7 (2026-07-09 16:32 +0200, same author, 'Hhrr module (#258)') first adds app/Http/Requests/PayrollRequest.php with 'user_id' => 'required|exists:user,id' (git log --diff-filter=A confirms the add) and rewrites the index query inline, still with an unscoped base Payroll::where('period_year', $year). Later V2 Laravel-11 migration b03c8c6f (2024-11-01) preserved the unscoped disclosure shape; it is not an origin. Direct fix 59644f91 (2026-07-28 10:16 +0200, same author, PR #264, 'Fix/payroll cross tenant isolation') scopes the index base query by whereHas('user', company_id) (moving the company filter out of the optional employee branch), scopes PayrollRequest user_id with Rule::exists('user','id')->where('company_id',...), and bumps APP_VERSION 5.15.9 -> 5.15.10 (first fixed release v5.15.10; no later tag in local clone - v4.6.0/v5.5.3/v5.14.0 all contain the module without the fix). AI: both origins and the fix are by the repository's sole founding maintainer Gustavo Novaro with no AI trailers; repo convention calibrated (Claude Haiku 4.5 / copilot-swe-agent trailers appear elsewhere in history). NOT_AI supported.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Origin established: b7b362ae introduced src/lib/automations/engine.ts with the send_webhook action fetching account-controlled cfg.url with no SSRF guard (no isDeliverableUrl call, redirects followed by default); the immediate parent 66dd4ef97edfc734c423a4252bd4ebd19e1cff80 has no src/lib/automations/ directory, so this is the first write of the unguarded fetch. The guard (isDeliverableUrl in src/lib/webhooks/ssrf.ts) was added later by c0f390c for the separate webhook_endpoints delivery path, leaving the automation path unguarded until 7d1ddbf. Minimum remedy confirmed complete: 7d1ddbf routes send_webhook through isDeliverableUrl and adds redirect:'manual' plus a 10s timeout at the single fetch choke point, plus a link-local regression test; 23838a9 is only the PR #352 merge carrying that identical 51-line diff. This closes the SSRF across the vendor's execution and validation scope because validate.ts is a non-authoritative save-time mirror of runtime checks and the runtime fetch is the sole outbound request; no separate validate.ts SSRF guard is required.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Mechanism (locally verified in parcel-bundler/parcel clone .ai-slop/state/repos/parcel-bundler_parcel, GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1): BIC 81117b45f 'Parcel 2: V2 Server (#2817)' (single parent b463de11) introduces packages/reporters/dev-server/src/Server.js as a new file (git diff --name-status parent..BIC shows A for Server.js, dev-server/package.json; 26 added files). Server.js at BIC sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin '*' unconditionally with no Host or Origin validation (rg verifyHost/verifyOrigin/getDefaultAllowedHosts at BIC: zero matches), and HMRServer creates WebSocket.Server({server}) with its verifyClient origin check commented out, so a malicious page can connect/read cross-origin responses while a developer visits it (CWE-346). BIC/parent contrast: parent b463de11 has no packages/reporters/dev-server/ directory at all (git ls-tree empty; cat-file -e for Server.js fails), so the vulnerable v2 dev-server code is first-written here, not moved. Lifecycle boundary (v1 vs v2 kept distinct): the v1 line already shipped Access-Control-Allow-Origin '*' in src/Server.js at tags v1.6.0/v1.6.1 (Feb 2018; CORS commit ca84e1562 2018-02-14 first appears in merged-line tags parcel-bundler@1.11.0/1.12.0; GHSA range starts 1.6.1) — a separate, older v1 lifecycle; the v2 rewrite is BIC 81117b45f, first in release v2.0.0-alpha.0 (2019-05-23; parcel@2.0.0-alpha.1 2019-08-13 also contains it; v1.12.3 does not). Minimal fix (v2): 4bc56e324 'Verify Host and Origin headers in dev server' (2025-04-20T05:43:13Z) adds Host verification (getDefaultAllowedHosts/verifyHost) plus 403 on disallowed Host, restricts CORS to verified Origins, and adds ws verifyClient Origin validation; fix parent 40ebdcd87 still contains the wildcard CORS and lacks all verify* functions, so the diff is the minimum origin/host check. Fix-release boundary: no git tag contains 4bc56e324; it exists only on branch origin/fix-security and is NOT an ancestor of HEAD/v2.16.4; PR 10138 is CLOSED unmerged (GitHub PR page state CLOSED, mergedBy/mergedTime null). The v2-line mitigation is 9e2f6f137 'Add --no-cors option (#10268)' (2026-02-02, merged in v2.16.4): it adds an opt-in --no-cors flag (default CORS stays on) and does not reintroduce the origin checks, so origin validation remains absent from every released v2 tag (verified verifyHost/verifyOrigin absent in v2.14.4..v2.16.4 trees). GHSA-qm9p-f9j5-w83w (OSV) declares @parcel/reporter-dev-server >=1.6.1 fixed 2.16.4 via the --no-cors mitigation, but the 4bc56e324 origin/host hardening itself has no fixed release; treat fix date 2025-04-20 (commit author date on fix-security branch) and 'no released fixed version for the origin-check fix' as the resolved boundary. causal_research.bug_semantics: Mechanism: Gemini web_search provider (PR #13075) resolves Google grounding citation redirect URLs with parallel server-side HEAD requests in resolveRedirectUrl (fetch(url, {method:'HEAD', redirect:'follow'})), no SSRF guard, so attacker-influenced citation redirect targets can make the OpenClaw host fetch loopback/private/internal destinations (CWE-918). Verified lineage: local clone openclaw/openclaw (114k commits, no shallow). BIC a4c68d890 (author AkosCz, 2026-02-09 22:05:42 -0600, verified via GitHub commit page + .patch; parents:[c92c3ad224]) is the first write of runGeminiSearch/resolveRedirectUrl/REDIRECT_TIMEOUT: main parent 3f03cdea56 and PR parent c92c3ad224 web-search.ts both contain zero occurrences (830-line parent file checked via raw.githubusercontent), so parent is vulnerability-free. BIC landed on main 2026-02-23 as GitHub squash merge 3a3c2da916 (committer GitHub, squash aggregates several PR member commits). Intermediate hardening 5eb72ab769 (2026-02-24, Peter Steinberger) wrapped resolveRedirectUrl in fetchWithSsrFGuard but with TRUSTED_NETWORK_SSRF_POLICY={dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork:true} (trusted-network model), leaving private-network reachability - matches advisory wording 'private-network-allowing SSRF policy'; that commit is not the origin because the raw redirect-following HEAD fetch already reached private networks without any guard. Direct minimal fix 085c23ce (2026-03-02, Peter Steinberger): removes the dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork policy from the resolveRedirectUrl fetchWithSsrFGuard call so strict SSRF defaults (undici DNS lookup blocking localhost/metadata/private ranges) apply; 1-line code change plus docs/test/CHANGELOG. Release boundary verified with tags: v2026.2.26 contains BIC squash but not 085c23ce (affected); first fixed tag v2026.3.1 = d76b224e appcast commit 2026-03-02, contains 085c23ce; archive correctly flagged OSV 'fixed SHA' d76b224e as release metadata, not the security fix. AI evidence: BIC commit message has no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with/bot-email markers; named human author AkosCz. Trailer-convention calibration in the SAME PR is decisive here: squash 3a3c2da916 body shows Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com> Co-Authored-By attached to a later member commit ('fix: use structured readResponseText result in Gemini error path') and in the PR footer, while the introducer member commit a4c68d890 carries no AI trailer - i.e. the workflow did mark Claude contributions when present, so absence on the BIC is meaningful positive evidence rather than bare absence. Squash aggregate itself is not the BIC (its Claude trailer belongs to the non-introducer error-path commit). Claude-era timing (Feb 2026, repo has active AI-trailer convention) considered; verdict NOT_AI for the BIC stands, with the caveat that trailer absence cannot exclude undecorated AI drafting.

Direct fix 09e72c4fd8007277121ed48db63a124b112b96fe (2026-06-01, Norman Maurer, 'Wrapping plain trust manager silently disables hostname verification') makes the wrapping explicit/safe; sibling merges 0d4e608cde/3a023c0f9f are the same-day fork merges. Patched 4.1.135.Final / 4.2.15.Final. AI: BIC (2016) and fix are named-human Netty commits with no AI markers. NOT_AI.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Verified in the local clone. The vulnerability is an uncapped gas meter for before-send contract sudo calls in x/tokenfactory/keeper/before_send.go: the Token Factory import commit 6ae96fb (PR #186 in commit message, 2024-09-04, squashed under org account Mantrachain Development Support with 11 human Co-authored-by trailers and no AI tool trailers) added childCtx := c.WithGasMeter(types.TrackBeforeSendGasLimit), spending hook gas independently of remaining tx gas. Parent ff5eab2 has no x/ directory and no before_send.go, so first-write at BIC holds. The vulnerable code is a close port of Neutron tokenfactory (released 2023-11-28), whose v2.0.0 has the same callBeforeSendListener with sdk.NewGasMeter(types.TrackBeforeSendGasLimit); an interim Osmosis tokenfactory swap (2024-09-11) postdates the BIC and was reverted (2024-09-13), so it does not change BIC identity. Fix boundary: commit 30d36c4 (PR #437, 2025-09-05, Lance Lan Meng) caps the meter with min(BeforeSendHookGasLimit, GasRemaining); v4.0.2 (2025-09-08) additionally ships a stronger ProxyGasMeter rewrite (PR #433/#438 by yihuang). GHSA/OSV confirm affected <=4.0.1 and fixed in 4.0.2/5.0.0. AI role: negative - commit date 2024-09-04 predates mainstream agentic coding adoption, human coauthors, repo convention uses Co-authored-by for humans only, and the only AI-adjacent marker in the BIC message (coderabbit on genesis.go) touches a different file than the vulnerable one. The uncapped-meter pattern was inherited from upstream Neutron code, not generated in-repo. Supplied verdict NOT_AI is supported.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Spring Security authorization bypass for method-security annotations on private methods (@EnableMethodSecurity(mode=ASPECTJ) plus spring-security-aspects). Mechanism: BIC dc2e1af2 ('Align Method Traversal with MergedAnnotations', Closes gh-16751, GPG-signed, authored 2025-01-08, committed 2025-03-17) first writes the findMethod helper in core/src/main/java/org/springframework/security/core/annotation/UniqueSecurityAnnotationScanner.java: it replaces the parent's targetClass.getDeclaredMethod(name, parameterTypes) lookup (which does locate private methods) with a scan of targetClass.getDeclaredMethods() matching by identity 'candidate == method' or by isOverride(), and isOverride excludes private methods (!Modifier.isPrivate). A distinct Method reflection object for the same private method fails both branches, so the annotation is missed and authorization is skipped. Parent diff: tree 75b0e9f5 of parent 4993fa86 (a merge commit) contains no findMethod, no 'candidate == method' and no Modifier usage (0 grep hits), confirming the construct is introduced exactly in this commit. Minimal fix: bf2aaa1b ('Use .equals to Compare Methods', Closes gh-17143) changes exactly one functional line, 'candidate == method' to 'candidate.equals(method)', in UniqueSecurityAnnotationScanner.java (full tree diff is 2 files, the second a test-role tweak in PreAuthorizeAspectTests); the 6.5.x counterpart c972de53 first lands in 6.5.0.
