causal_research.bug_semantics:
NOT_AI, independently verified with affirmative first-party evidence.

MECHANISM (CWE-918 SSRF, CVSS v4.0 8.7): @angular/ssr createRequestUrl builds the request URL with the two-arg native URL constructor new URL(path, base). A request path starting with a double slash is parsed by the URL constructor as a schema-relative URL, so the security-intended base (protocol, host, port) is discarded and the attacker-controlled hostname embedded in the path wins; the SSR document virtual location (DOCUMENT / PlatformLocation) resolves to that external domain, and any later relative request during SSR (e.g. HttpClient.get-of-assets-data-json) is sent to the attacker server.

BIC FIRST-WRITE (positive evidence, not absence-only): 3c9697a8 is the FIRST commit creating packages/angular/ssr/src/request.ts including createRequestUrl returning new URL(url, base); its only parent ad4c782e (v18.2.0-rc.0 release-notes commit by Charles Lyding) contains NO request.ts and NO createRequestUrl helper anywhere in the tree (parent packages/angular/ssr/src holds only common-engine.ts, inline-css-processor.ts, peformance-profiler.ts), so the vulnerable enabling code is positively introduced by 3c9697a8, not merely hardened.

INTERVENING COMMITS NON-INTRODUCING: c7fc9190 (relocate Node.js Request/Response helpers to /node entry point) is a pure move keeping the two-arg constructor; 481ccdb only changes url to (originalUrl ?? url) keeping the two-arg constructor; established via git log --follow on packages/angular/ssr/node/src/request.ts.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CAUSE: GitProxy (BIC 8cec7591, 'wip', 2020-05-31) parses the client receive-pack ref-update line into commitFrom/commitTo (parsePush.js: action.setCommit(messageParts[0].substr(4), messageParts[1])) and writePack.js pipes the ENTIRE client request body ('input: req.body') to 'git receive-pack'. Nothing validates that every commit object in the client pack is reachable from the advertised newOid, so extra commits in the pack are written to the upstream repo and remain fetchable by direct SHA even though no branch points at them (silent exfiltration; GHSA-v98g-8rqx-g93g, CWE-345). BIC/PARENT CONTRAST: parent 01d337a7 has no proxy/processors or writePack path at all; BIC introduces the proxy push chain and this gap in one 'wip' commit, so 8cec7591 is the true BIC and the parent contains none of the vulnerable receive-pack/audit pipeline. MINIMAL FIX: the initial 'feat: add check for hidden commits' 9c1449f4 (Fabio Vincenzi, 2025-05-16) was INCOMPLETE ON ITS OWN: it never landed on main before the security merge (merge-base --is-ancestor 9c1449f4 d4d9239a = false), it only detected pack commits outside oldOid..newOid, and it did not persist newIdxFiles or fix parsePush. The terminal security change is fork-merge a620a2f33 ('Merge commit from fork', Thomas Cooper, 2025-07-30, parents d4d9239a + 60e77d1c): (1) writePack.ts now snapshots .idx files before/after receive-pack and stores action.newIdxFiles; (2) chain.ts inserts checkHiddenCommits between writePack and checkIfWaitingAuth; (3) the rewritten checkHiddenCommits.ts fails the push when any commit in the new idx files is outside the introduced rev-list range; (4) parsePush (394-line diff, incl. 93a6123c capability parsing, co-authored Thomas Cooper) and getMissingData harden the same surface. 9c1449f4 and the fork-branch line it heads (1fd86acb idx tracking, 334c967e UpdatedRef/newIdxFiles in Action, 00287432 empty-branch-push guard, 93a6123c parsePush capability parsing) are the incomplete-first-fix boundary that the merge folds in; 12fce21a (1.19.2 package.json bump) is a release marker, not a fix. The merged security state first ships in v1.19.2 (git tag --contains a620a2f33 -> v1.19.2; GHSA: affected <= 1.19.1, patched 1.19.2 and 2.0.0). AI EVIDENCE: no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with/Copilot/Cursor/Claude/GPT marker on BIC 8cec7591 or anywhere in the last 40 security-fix commits on the fork branch; BIC author == committer grovesy (Paul Groves). causal_research.bug_semantics: Mechanism: getDiff.js treated commitFrom == 0000...0 as a brand-new branch and diffed the pushed commits against the empty tree (4b825dc...), so a new branch b cut from an unapproved commit on branch a could be approved on b and later pushed back to a without that parent-lineage commit ever being policy-checked (advisory GHSA-39p2-8hq9-fwj6, CVE-2025-54585: 'new branch approval exploit'; getDiff.ts and parsePush.ts both zero-SHA branches named). BIC vs parent: 879e26c8 (grovesy, 2020-10-12, 'working on diffs on new branches') is the first commit that creates the zero-SHA branch: its only change is getDiff.js, and its new code 'if (action.commitFrom == 0000...0) { if (commitData[0].parent != 0000...0) cmd = git diff <parent> <commitTo> } else cmd = git diff <commitFrom> <commitTo>' is exactly the advisory-named zero-SHA handling; parent b9e1dc8 (2020-10-12) always used the empty-tree fallback 'git diff 4b825dc... HEAD' for new branches, which ignores commitFrom/commitTo but has no parent-boundary branch. Follow-up 66285509 (same day, same author) changed commitData[0].parent to commitData[len-1].parent in getDiff and made parsePush set commitFrom = last-commit parent on zero SHA; both zero-SHA branches existed on main by v1.0.0, so the advisory-specific parent-boundary mechanism was active in all affected releases. causal_research.bug_semantics: Mechanism: the plugin ships a Vite dev-server middleware (apply: serve; wired in configureServer in src/serve.ts; no build path). Commit d9cd9ba6 (Fix: directory copy not working during dev, 2022-04-06, sapphi-red <green@sapphi.red>) added a second lookup loop to viaLocal() in src/middleware.ts: for the first fileMap directory key that the request URI starts with, it returns resolve(root, val.src, uri.slice(dir.length)) and serves it via statSync/toHeaders. uri derives from the raw request URL with only decodeURIComponent, query/import stripping, and leading-slash trimming, so traversal segments such as ../ or %2e%2e%2f reach uri.slice(dir.length); resolve() then normalizes them outside val.src, and the result is served without any containment check. BIC vs parent 04f57951: parent viaLocal is map-get only (fileMap.get(uri) -> resolve(root, file)) with no directory-prefix resolve path; the vulnerable slice(dir.length) resolve plus serve-on-stat first appears in d9cd9ba6. Minimal fix: 0bc6b49ed (main, parent 148950790) and its v2 backport 4627afb8 (parent 08cafec9, exactly the vite-plugin-static-copy@2.3.1 tag commit) add isFileInside(filepath, srcBase) (srcBase-with-trailing-sep prefix check) and return undefined when resolve(srcBase, uri.slice(dir.length)) escapes srcBase; both diffs are identical at this resolution point, confirming minimality; message: fix: only serve files under src (#195). Authors: both fixes authored by 翠 <green@sapphi.red>, the same human maintainer identity as the BIC (sapphi-red/green@sapphi.red); 0bc6b49 committed via GitHub web flow, 4627afb committed by sapphi-red. Git trailers on BIC and both fixes contain no AI markers (no Co-Authored-By/im/generated), and positive AI evidence on the BIC itself is absent; exclusion rests on these active checks (single human identity across BIC and fix, 2022 commit), not on marker silence alone. Version boundaries verified in git: BIC is ancestor of tags from v0.4.3 (first containing tag) through vite-plugin-static-copy@4.1.1; vulnerable slice(dir.length) line present at tags 2.3.1 and 3.1.1; guard present at 2.3.2 and 3.1.2. Exposure precondition: only a running Vite dev server using this plugin with a directory copy target; the middleware serves requests on the dev-server origin and build output is not exposed through it. Remediation boundary matches the advisory (GHSA-pp7p-q8fx-2968 global page): affected >=0.4.3,<=2.3.1 and >=3.0.0,<=3.1.1; patched 2.3.2 and 3.1.2. Attribution accepted: root cause is the human-written 2022 directory-prefix serving loop d9cd9ba6, not AI-generated code.

round17_research.reasoning: The decisive question is closed: first-party vendor patch scope and affected/fixed versions are recovered, so the case is no longer an EVIDENCE_GAP. CVE-2025-47110 is a published (not withdrawn) Adobe CNA record, stored XSS via server-side template injection (CWE-79, CVSS 8.4/9.1, PR:H). The sink is Magento\Email\Model\Template\Filter::blockDirective(): {{block class=...}}/{{block id=...}} directives create a layout block, copy attacker-controlled params via setDataUsingMethod, and call toHtml() with no unique cache_key, so attacker-controlled markup is cached under the same key as layout-rendered blocks (admin menu) and served to other high-privilege sessions. Adobe's isolated patch VULN-31609_2.4.X.patch and the KA-27181/APSB25-50 release notes name the exact fix: pin cache_key after params are applied. That patch is byte-identical to public develop commit AC-14694 b535da75725601a520f0734065a9b294d69ca115 (Binh Tran, 2025-05-20), and the identical hunk appears in all fixed tags 2.4.8-p1/2.4.7-p6/2.4.6-p11/2.4.5-p13 (absent from 2.4.8/2.4.7-p5/2.4.6-p10/2.4.5-p12). The smallest public first-write of the defective blockDirective is 4bdbf6b6ebc4b53dbde9483df745cfca7e864a36 (2011-12-02, author/committer mage2-team <mage2-team@magento.com>, 'Merged commits from the original repository.'), a single-parent import whose immediate parent be09cb921bafae2d06302f3f9c9ecacaf90da6dd contains only LICENSE.txt and no Filter.php. That 2011 commit has no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with/AI trailer and predates LLM coding assistants. Attribution is therefore NOT_AI (human Magento core-team BIC, no AI marker on the introducing object). Minor non-causal note: Adobe's APSB25-50 vulnerability table labels CVE-2025-47110 'Reflected XSS' while CVE.org, GHSA and KA-27181 all describe 'stored XSS via SSTI'; the isolated-patch mechanism (block cache_key pin) is the stored/persistent form.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Netty MQTT5 decoder unbounded variable-header property parsing (CVE-2026-44248 / GHSA-jfg9-48mv-9qgx): MQTT5 support (PR #10483) added decodeProperties and variable-header property parsing that runs before the existing maxBytesInMessage body-size check, so a maliciously large property block is parsed without hitting the configured message-size cap (unbounded memory/CPU). BIC verified in local netty__netty clone: be2cd68443 (2020-08-31, Paul Lysak, MQTT5 support for netty-codec-mqtt #10483), parent fde6bc8885 (unrelated NetUtils commit; no MQTT5 property parsing in its tree), so the maxBytesInMessage bypass originates here; the MQTT3-era parent decoder lacked a Properties section entirely. Fix: 4.2-line fork-merge 82f47fa5 and 4.1 backport 1986c38c (both 2026-05-04, Chris Vest), restore the sizing bound; fixed by tag 4.1.133.Final / 4.2.13.Final (OSV listed-release SHAs b3844c81/fb13125f are release-prepare commits, not the decoder patch). causal_research.bug_semantics: HTTP request smuggling / parser desync in Netty chunked encoding (GHSA-pwqr-wmgm-9rr8): the HTTP chunk-size line parser terminated the line at the first CR or LF and parsed the chunk size with Integer.valueOf(hex,16) without validating chunk-extension bytes, so a crafted chunk-extension containing CR/LF could desynchronize Netty's parser from an upstream proxy/server (request smuggling class). Verified in local clone netty__netty: BIC 4ac032c6 (2008-11-19, Trustin Lee, 'Merged the HTTP branch into the trunk', single parent e29ba2ee) is the first write of HttpMessageDecoder with READ_CHUNK_SIZE - the parent has no HTTP codec at all, so the vulnerable stop-at-first-CR/LF line reader is born here. Later 2009 commits (44498e06, 66423e0c) added semicolon extension delimiters but still terminated at the first CRLF; the 2013 HttpObjectDecoder overhaul b7de8680 is a rewrite/move of the same pattern, not the origin. Direct fix 60e53c99 (2026-03-24, Chris Vest, 'Stricter HTTP/1.1 chunk extension parsing (#16537)', parent 9f47a7b6) introduces HttpChunkLineValidatingByteProcessor, the first code that rejects illegal bytes (including CR/LF) inside chunk-ext. Release boundary by tag ancestry: earliest Netty tags containing the fix are netty-4.1.132.Final and later 4.1.x line (4.1.131 and earlier do not contain it). OSV SHAs 4cc98736/ec119d48 are release tags, not the parser change. AI: BIC is 2008 work by Netty's founder Trustin Lee, decades before AI-assist; fix by named human maintainer Chris Vest; no AI markers anywhere in the lineage. NOT_AI supported; residual note: the advisory's chunk-extension delimiter behavior arrived in 2009 commits, but the stop-at-first-CR/LF origin is unambiguously the 2008 first write.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Mechanism: devalue.parse deserialized attacker-controlled JSON into a hydration loop that assigned every object key verbatim (object[key] = get_value(n)) with no key allowlist. A payload key of __proto__ therefore assigned a prototype onto the target object, and a non-numeric string index in an array-position reference could reach get_value with an out-of-range or type-mismatched accessor. BIC/parent comparison verified in local git: parent 4c231ac parse.js was still the literal stub 'return TODO'; BIC 46ee86e (WIP parse, Rich Harris, 2022-10-03, authored and committed by hello@rich-harris.dev) was the first commit to introduce the key-assignment hydration loop into src/parse.js, plus the initial index-get_value path. No earlier commit in the repo writes this loop. Minimal fix: 0623a47 (Merge commit from fork, 2025-08-26, author Rich Harris rich.harris@vercel.com, committer GitHub noreply@github.com, GPG-signed) patched src/parse.js with exactly two additions: (1) tightened get_value guard to throw Invalid input when typeof index !== number (closing the non-numeric-index path), and (2) added an explicit key === __proto__ throw before the key-assignment loop (closing the prototype-pollution path). Both aspects retained. Fix diff also adds two changeset entries (rich-clouds-walk: disallow __proto__ properties on objects; huge-ads-study: disallow array method access when parsing) and two regression tests. The fix commit is a squash-merge (single parent 02d20e8a, no second-parent SHA recoverable from the merge object) whose sole visible fork member is the squashed commit itself; no finer public fork-member commit is reachable from the local clone (--all --no-tags), so finer member recovery is not possible without the (rate-limited, disallowed) GitHub PR listing API. AI exclusion: git log -1 --format=%B on both BIC and fix shows no Co-Authored-By, Generated-By, Claude, Copilot, OpenAI, Anthropic, or other AI-attribution trailers. This is positive absence evidence, not an inference from marker absence alone: the BIC is a 2022 WIP commit by a known human maintainer with a personal email, predating mainstream AI-assisted commit tooling adoption, and the fix is a manually authored patch by the same maintainer using a work email, GPG-signed via GitHub. Human author confirmed on both commits. Version boundary: advisory GHSA-vj54-72f3-p5jv / CVE-2025-57820 states affected < 5.3.2, patched 5.3.2. Verified locally: tag v5.3.1 points to 7e2b201 (parent 02d20e8); tag v5.3.2 points to 86a6a66 (direct child of 0623a47). Thus the vulnerability window spans from 46ee86e (first hydration loop, pre-3.x era) through all releases before v5.3.2.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Traefik Postgres provider TCP handling DoS (GHSA-89p3-4642-cr2w): connection read/write deadlines were removed on the TCP-passthrough path serving Postgres (and the fix comment confirms the deadline existed to prevent hanging connections while waiting for the client), so a client that opens the Postgres route and stalls before STARTTLS/ClientHello can hold the connection/goroutine unbounded - enabling resource exhaustion. Verified in local clone traefik__traefik: BIC 15973f55 (2024-05-06 15:46 +0200, Romain rtribotte, subject Remove deadlines when handling PostgreSQL connections, single parent a4150409) modifies pkg/server/router/tcp/router.go adding SetDeadline(time.Time{}) clearing on the dispatch path (diff shows the clearing block added at ServeTCP line 123+); its parent lacked that clearing on the postgres path, i.e. the pre-BIC arming behavior bounded the wait, while the BIC is the first state with the unbounded wait. Direct fix 31e566e9 (2026-02-11 09:48 +0100, Romain, subject Remove conn deadline after STARTTLS negociation, Co-authored-by Michael <michael.matur@gmail.com> - human traefik maintainer) moves the logic: servePostgres keeps/sets a deadline while reading STARTTLS and ClientHello and clears it only after negotiation (postgres.go), while router.go drops the blanket clearing - diff comments explicitly say the deadline prevented hanging connections while waiting for the client. Release boundary by tag ancestry: earliest tag containing the fix is v3.6.8 (v3.6.x series onward; no v2.11 backport present) matching advisory fixed-in v3.6.8; OSV GIT fixed 2f215ab9 is the Prepare release v3.6.8 changelog commit, not the patch. AI: BIC and fix are 2024/2026 named traefik maintainer work with human co-author, no AI trailers. NOT_AI supported.

causal_research.bug_semantics: PhpSpreadsheet file-existence/protocol handling flaw (GHSA-q4q6-r8wh-5cgh): file open/read paths called is_file() / file-existence checks on user-controlled filenames WITHOUT first prohibiting stream wrappers (php://, phar://, data://, etc.), so a caller supplying a wrapper path could cause the reader to fetch/read remote or wrapper-backed content unexpectedly (SSRF/arbitrary-file-read-adjacent / protocol injection class). Direct fix 93c94eb3 (2026-04-04, oleibman, 'Merge commit from fork' titled 'Test Protocol Not Supplied Before Using is_file', parent 36013a3d) adds prohibitWrappers() invoked from assertFile()/testFileNoThrow() paths - diff touches src/PhpSpreadsheet/Helper/Downloader.php, IOFactory.php, Reader/Xml.php, Shared/File.php plus regression test NoPharTest.php. AI: BIC is 2016 work by named PhpSpreadsheet maintainer Adrien Crivelli with no AI markers; fix by named human oleibman (Co-authored-by reporter calligraf0 - reporting credit, not generation). causal_research.bug_semantics: Causal chain independently confirmed by local git. MECHANISM: pathProxy.ts getProxyTarget() interpolated req.params.port directly into the proxy target URL (`http://0.0.0.0:${req.params.port}...`). Node url.parse treats `@` as an authority separator, so a /proxy/test@evil.com/path request resolved to target hostname evil.com with userinfo 0.0.0.0:test - an unintended-proxy confused-deputy (CWE-441) that leaked the code-server session cookie to an attacker-controlled host. BIC/PARENT CONTRAST: parent 4b6cbacb (src/node/http.ts proxyRequest) called parseInt(options.port, 10) and threw an HttpError on isNaN before building http(s)://127.0.0.1:${port}; BIC 112eda46 ('Convert routes to Express', 2020-10-20) rewrote routes and dropped that validation, introducing the raw template-literal pathProxy target. MINIMUM FIX: 47d6d3ad wraps req.params.port in parseInt(..., 10) and throws HttpCode.BadRequest on invalid port - narrowing the accepted value back to a number. Follow-up 9bd3b83e (2025-05-08, Asher) replaced the try/catch with an explicit isNaN check because parseInt returns NaN rather than throwing; the as-merged 47d6d3ad form does not throw for 'test@evil.com' (parseInt -> NaN is silently injected), but url.parse('http://0.0.0.0:NaN/...') does not produce an attacker-controlled hostname, so the destructive confusion is still closed at 47d6d3ad and the NaN guard is a hardening follow-up. AI EVIDENCE: no Generated-with/Copilot/Claude/Cursor/GPT trailers on BIC or fix (commit messages and raw .patch checked); PR #7337 body has no AI attribution; author of both BIC and fix is human (Asher <ash@coder.com> BIC, Kyle Carberry <kyle@carberry.com> fix commit). Verdict NOT_AI retained. VERSION BOUNDARY: BIC contained in v3.10.0 and v4.99.3, absent before 2020-10-20; fix 47d6d3ad first appears in tag v4.99.4 (tagged directly on the fix commit, 2025-05-02), so affected range is < 4.99.4, matching CVE record and GHSA-p483-wpfp-42cj.

However, none of these directly wrote the vulnerable behavior of accepting shell wrapper segments without inline-command recursion.
round3_research.flaw_origin: Shell wrapper segments were matched by their wrapper executable path alone; no recursive evaluation of inline compound commands existed before fix 8d81e76f230.
round3_research.reasoning: Direct fix identified and confirmed. The chain of wrapper-resolution refactors obscures the original writer.
round3_research.remaining_gap: Trace src/infra/exec-approvals-analysis.ts back past 81fbfa06eef to its initial creation to find the first commit that evaluated shell wrapper segments by wrapper executable without inline-command recursion.

Affected range 4.2.0.Final .. 4.2.13.Final (CVE range starts at 4.2.0.Final; 4.2.0 release is the pom-bump 09e64d25). Direct fix 0ec3d97fab (2026-04-25, Norman Maurer, PR #16689, parent 1b77808f) corrects the mask-0 handling in that registration path; port to main is 538a21ce3e (2024-05-22). OSV lists b3844c81 as the 4.2.13 release tag (not the patch). AI: BIC is 2024 work by a named Netty maintainer with no AI markers; fix also by Norman Maurer 2026, no AI trailers. NOT_AI supported.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Decisive question answered: the Cursor-coauthored change created the advisory-specific personal-agent trust-boundary exposure, and the defect lies in the NEW integration rather than solely in the pre-existing helper. The raw HTTP client bypassing n8n SSRF protection pre-existed in searxngSearch, but it was only admin/config-reachable; buildFallbackWebSearchTool is the new code that fed a user-controlled credential.apiUrl into that client, which is the personal-agent SSRF the advisory targets. The fix (ca3d42d838 squash bundle) confirms the split: it injects createWebSearchFetch(outboundHttp, ssrfConfig, ssrfProtectionService) as a policy-aware fetchImpl through buildFallbackWebSearchTool into searxngSearch (closing the 2.34.1 personal-agent lineage), and separately rewrites the older ToolSearXng node off LangChain SearxngSearch onto ctx.helpers.httpRequest (closing the 2.33.4 2.0.0-era tool lineage). This is AI new-exposure contribution on a mixed human+AI commit, consistent with the supplied verdict narrowed to personal-agent exposure.

BIC and root boundary (local git in the free5gc/nssf clone): 51bef82fba8e2934e6bbe3d46e2afc928c75f417 ("Init commit", author free5gc-org <free5gc.org@gmail.com>, 2020-04-28) has no parent, i.e. bic_parent is null; git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD returns exactly two unrelated roots, 4ce53ee ("Release v1.0.0", 2020-02-07) and 51bef82, with no merge base, and git log --all -S "Expiry.IsZero()" shows the pattern was introduced only in those two root commits. Both roots contain the identical unguarded pattern (51bef82 at nssf_producer/nssaiavailability_subscription.go:64 on the master lineage; 4ce53ee at producer/nssaiavailability_subscription.go:73 on the main lineage that anchors every tag v1.0.0-v1.4.5), so no in-repo introduction commit exists and the earliest representable BIC on the audited lineage is the root itself. Minimal fix: 66fc727a894fa821fde14030346b18de69192204 (author and committer leowu0407 <leo31739061@gmail.com>, 2025-08-15 09:21:46 +0000, parent 3bb6990) touches one file and one line, changing "if !subscription.SubscriptionData.Expiry.IsZero()" to "if subscription.SubscriptionData.Expiry != nil && !subscription.SubscriptionData.Expiry.IsZero()" at internal/sbi/processor/nssaiavailability_subscription.go:80; the parent 3bb6990 still contains the unguarded line, confirming the fix is minimal and directly closes this mechanism (the later ae1d5d6 of 2026-01-11 adds an RWMutex against a data race in the same handler family and is outside this mechanism). AI attribution: raw commit objects (git cat-file -p) of 51bef82 and 66fc727 contain no Co-Authored-By, Signed-off-by, Generated, Claude, Copilot or other coding-assistant markers, but marker absence alone is not treated as proof; the affirmative non-AI evidence is that the BIC is a 2020-04-28 project bootstrap commit authored by the free5gc-org service identity before LLM coding assistants were in ecosystem use, with Expiry deriving its *time.Time type from the imported openapi model rather than from AI-suggested code shape, and the fix author leowu0407 has an independent multi-year manual commit trail in the same repo under the same identity (e.g. 4a5a428 2025-02-04 and 9d7d77f 2025-02-03, targeted resource-URI bug fixes, plus the merge 002ee94 of 2025-01-02 co-authored under their GitHub noreply identity), and the fix itself is a one-line targeted nil guard in the repo conventional-commit style. causal_research.bug_semantics: Mechanism: HeaderWriterFilter (Spring Security headers feature, incl. cache-control headers) wraps the response in HeaderWriterResponse extends OnCommittedResponseWrapper; with the default shouldWriteHeadersEagerly=false, header writers run only when the wrapper detects response commit. Commit detection tracks Content-Length by overriding addHeader and setContentLength/setContentLengthLong only; Content-Length set via setHeader/setIntHeader/addIntHeader bypassed tracking, so the body could be committed and headers written too late or not at all, opening responses to data exposure via caches (spring.io advisory CVE-2026-22732/GHSA-mf92-479x-3373; underlying spring-framework#36381; severity CRITICAL). BIC (independently verified): 08b1b56e2cd5ad72126f4bbeb15a47d9b104dfff, 2015-07-14, SEC-2973 Add OnCommittedResponseWrapper by Rob Winch (author=committer, rwinch@gopivotal.com), created web/.../context/OnCommittedResponseWrapper.java with ONLY addHeader/setContentLength overrides; parent 316886affc432daccfe04214ec259480a1e99a54 lacks the class (git log -1 P field and commit patch page: new file, no earlier content). The archive's historical-regression alternative is resolved: a content scan of the class across 173 release tags (4.0.2.RELEASE through 7.0.3) found the three missing overrides in NO released version before the fix (only in 6.5.9+, 7.0.4+ tags, which validates scan sensitivity), so the omission was continuous from the 2015 first write; 08b1b56 remains the minimal introducing commit. Fix (independently verified): 1dae9aa459436e0bb1a95701ed0d31e12be7788a, 2026-02-24, Add Missing OnCommitedResponseWrapper Header Overrides, Robert Winch (author=committer), single-parent atomic commit (parent bec25edeb050b6bb917f8fb3dbb89b8c3d480959) adding setHeader/setIntHeader/addIntHeader overrides and refactoring addHeader to shared checkContentLength helpers plus three new tests; Closes gh-18797. Same commit object is an ancestor of tags 6.5.9 and 7.0.4 (both released 2026-03-16; git merge-base --is-ancestor exit 0), matching OSS fix boundary 6.5.9/7.0.4; 6.4.15/6.3.15/5.8.24/5.7.22 are enterprise-only patches and shouldWriteHeadersEagerly=true is the documented workaround. AI evidence on BIC: positive and negative - 2015 predates AI code assistants; author+committer is Rob Winch, named human Spring Security lead (Javadoc @author); gopivotal corporate email; SEC-2973-era commit with no trailer, consistent with 2015 repo convention (no trailers then; Closes gh-xxxx trailers only appear later, 4219 repo-wide). Calibration shows the repo does carry Co-Authored-By AI trailers (e.g. Claude) on some 2026-03 commits, yet the 2026 fix carries none; absence of trailers is therefore corroborated by era, identity and repository convention rather than used alone. Verdict: supplied NOT_AI confirmed; no AI role on the BIC.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Causal mechanism (authorization-context interaction now resolved): CVE-2025-49594 is a cross-user token-minting flaw (CWE-285) in the OIDC provider template userapplications.vm. At BIC f8b522c (OIDC-229, 2025-04-30 16:25 +02:00), token operations were retargeted from the authenticated caller ($xcontext.userReference) to the viewed profile ($doc.documentReference) for both addConsent and getConsents, while the surrounding guard remained: if caller != viewed profile AND !hasAccess('programming') then deny. The one-argument hasAccess('programming') does not take the (caller, target) pair; for a VIEW-only visitor of another user's profile it evaluates the programming right in the wrong scope (document/page-author context instead of the visiting subject) and returns true, so the guard passes and addConsent($doc.documentReference, ...) mints an access token for the viewed user. The template evaluates this guard before every action path (line 36, then addConsent at line 67 inside the #else branch), so the UI gate is the user-facing control; the backend script addConsent's AccessDeniedException for script author is defense in depth, not the bypassed layer. With token authentication enabled, any VIEW-able profile becomes impersonable. BIC vs parent (local git, blob-complete clone, GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH): parent 18ae19e (merge PR #81, same day) still calls addConsent($xcontext.userReference)/getConsents($xcontext.userReference) — self-targeted only; even with the dead guard (typo hasAcess since OIDC-195 040eb6c, 2024-10-02) viewing another profile could not mint that user's token. f8b522c is the first commit that both retargets to the viewed profile and makes the guard actually evaluate (typo fix hasAcess→hasAccess). git log -S confirms 'doc.documentReference' enters this template only at 040eb6c (as guard RHS, not as consent target) and reaches addConsent/getConsents first at f8b522c. OSV's introduced 46f78862c24fa2df959293bdb58fd148fc0cfda1 is '[maven-release-plugin] prepare release oidc-2.17.1' (2025-04-30), a version-range marker, not the bug-introducing change. Minimal fix: d90d717 (OIDC-240, 2025-06-12 11:16 +02:00) changes the single template line to three-argument hasAccess('programming', $xcontext.userReference, $doc.documentReference), explicitly binding the check to the exact (caller, target) pair and removing the self-targeting exemption that the one-arg call inadvertently granted to cross-profile viewers; adds integration test asserting a guest visiting another user's profile cannot access token management (OIDCTest asserts OIDCApplicationsUserProfilePage.isAllowed() is false before login, plus pageobject helper @since 2.18.2). Three files, +32/-6 lines, template check is the sole behavioral change; nothing else regresses OIDC-229's legitimate programming-right feature. Positive NOT_AI attribution evidence (independent of marker absence): (1) JIRA OIDC-229 (https://jira.xwiki.org/browse/OIDC-229) was filed by tmortagne (thomas.mortagne@xwiki.com, matching commit author/committer Thomas Mortagne) at 2025-04-30T16:11:30+02:00 — 14 minutes before the BIC commit at 16:25:14+02:00 — with first-person description 'That was the intent of the code, but looks like I did not tested that use case...', a self-documented intent-vs-implementation gap predating the vulnerable commit. (2) Repo-level AI-trailer convention calibrated: three commits (131bf6e, d71eafe, 1b888ca, all 2026-08-19, 16 months after BIC) carry byte-exact 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>' trailers in their commit bodies; BIC f8b522c and fix d90d717 bodies contain no such trailer (checked with cat -A at byte level). This gives trailer absence real probative weight here: the convention existed in the same repo and postdates the audited commits. (3) Commit shape matches interactive human work: single-file 4+/4- template edit bundling a typo fix with a retarget, author==committer, and the same maintainer has continuous repo history since the first commit on 2016-03-25. Together the JIRA-report→commit identity chain, the maintainer's own first-person intent admission, and the calibrated trailer convention affirmatively support human authorship. Vulnerable range is therefore >= 2.17.1 and < 2.18.2, fixed in 2.18.2, matching CVE-2025-49594 (CWE-285), GHSA-f2hf-pfrj-vrm7, NVD, and OSV, with the documented workaround 'disable token access'.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Mechanism: CVE-2025-55304 (GHSA-m54q-mm9w-fp6g) is a denial-of-service from quadratic ICC profile reassembly in JpegBase::readMetadata (src/jpgimage.cpp): each JPEG APP2 'ICC_PROFILE' chunk triggered a full buffer rebuild (allocate iccProfile_.size_+chunk, memcpy prior profile, memcpy chunk, setIccProfile), so N chunks cost quadratic copies. BIC/parent contrast independently verified in local git: parent 9d060816 has no incremental ICC accumulation - it skips APP2 payloads during the marker scan and recovers the whole profile in one printStructure(kpsIccProfile) pass afterwards; BIC 3d57bbc6 (Robin Mills, 2016-09-12, '#1074 Work in progress... icc-test.sh is broken') first writes DataBuf profile(iccProfile_.size_+icc.size_) with the prior+chunk memcpy and setIccProfile per chunk. 'git log -S 'extend existing profile' --reverse -- src/jpgimage.cpp' returns 3d57bbc6 as the first commit introducing that code, so the 2016 first-write claim is verified, not just source-reported. Later rewrites (483a1497 2021, DataBuf std::copy/std::copy_n migration b9f9d041/ae4df712 2022) restructure but do not remove the quadratic accumulation. Minimal fix: 472d55ede19e07e09fcd45644cd963a5cf31b49d (Kevin Backhouse, 2025-08-15; committed by Rosen Penev 2025-08-19) adds Image::appendIccProfile()/checkIccProfile() and replaces the per-chunk rebuild with iccProfile_.resize(start+size) + memcpy of only the new chunk (amortized linear; 3 files, +32/-14). AI markers: none on BIC or fix - git log --format=%B shows no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with/Copilot/Claude trailers. Positive attribution beyond absent trailers: BIC is authored by long-time exiv2 maintainer Robin Mills in Sep 2016, before LLM coding assistants existed (affirmative temporal exclusion, not merely absence of markers); the fix is authored by GitHub Security Lab researcher Kevin Backhouse, who published the GHSA advisory under his own account, with PR #3335 (main, merged as eceaa0790a2b4d204dd2b75032d00ca2b4283cdc by neheb) and backport PR #3345 (0.28.x, merged as d6c67cdd39970795d078bd8ae457af27bf035296 via mergify branch, commit e5bf22e0cebeabeb2ffd40678344467a271be12d, merged 2025-08-23) all attributable to him. Version boundary: GHSA states affected <= 0.28.5, patched in 0.28.6; git merge-base checks confirm BIC 3d57bbc6 is in tags v0.28.5 and v0.28.6, the fix commit 472d55e is on main only (NOT an ancestor of v0.28.6), and the 0.28.x backport d6c67cdd IS an ancestor of tag v0.28.6 (commit 4654b52fb2026d1565570dbe411017d9431a7f40, 2025-08-29). The source report's note is confirmed: 4654b52 is the release tag commit (merge of PR #3366 'Release Exiv2 version 0.28.6'), not the security change itself; the security change shipped in v0.28.6 via backport merge d6c67cdd.

The object-level route parameter {fee_invoice} is therefore gated only by school membership and a generic permission, with no owner/guardian/relationship check: any same-school holder of 'read fee invoice' can read any student's invoice by ID (CWE-639 same-school IDOR). This is an application-wide origin problem, not a school-isolation bug: BIC itself correctly scopes list/create paths by users.school_id, and no guardian/staff-scoped policy variant exists anywhere in the code at BIC, tag V2.6.4, or HEAD. BIC/parent comparison: parent b5b9d825 'Changed timetable button size' (same author) has zero FeeInvoice controller/policy/model/routes/views paths (tree grep count 0); BIC adds all of them (controller, policy, model, service, migrations, seeder, factories, views, routes, tests) in one 42-file, +1459/-26 commit. Minimum fix: strengthen view() with owner/guardian-scoped checks after the school-scope precondition; no such fix exists on main. Unmerged branch modernization/domain-slices commit 7ac395937ca4 'fix portal role boundaries and invoice replay' (2026-09-03, Marvellous) does implement it: view() keeps permission+current-school gate but then requires student->student_record_id == $user->studentRecord->id, parent->child-link exists() through parent_records.user_id, and blocks portal-only roles from viewAny() via isPortalOnly(), with a new child-scoped portal invoices screen (17 files, +453/-54). causal_research.bug_semantics: Independently verified in the local exiv2 clone (GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1, node 1): BIC 8bd69f7c (#689 'Added support for DOS EPS files', vog, 2011-06-24, parent 0f1d1fc9) is the first write of DOS EPS section parsing into readWriteEpsMetadata; its parent has only '// TODO: Add support for DOS EPS (C5 D0 D3 C6)' and no posEps/posWmf/posTiff parsing, so the vulnerable code first appears here. Mechanism: the BIC family parses attacker-controlled header fields (posEps, posEndEps = getULong(...)+posEps, posWmf/sizeWmf, posTiff/sizeTiff) and validates them with unscaled arithmetic 'posX < 30 || posX + sizeX > size' / 'posEndEps > size'; on the write path the checked offsets are then used unchecked to memcpy whole sections out of the mmap ('writeTemp(tempIo, data + posWmf, sizeWmf)' at epsimage.cpp:1009 in the fix parent), so a size/offset that wraps or underflows the comparison (e.g. uint32_t sizeX such that posX+sizeX wraps; posX+sizeX was computed in 64-bit size_t for posX but sizeX is uint32_t since vog's own 115ba5a0 narrowed the declarations) passes the check and makes MemIo::write read far past the mapping. GHSA-496f-x7cq-cq39 stack trace confirms OOB read in MemIo::write <- writeTemp <- readWriteEpsMetadata (epsimage.cpp:1009) <- Exiv2::EpsImage::writeMetadata <- 'exiv2 -d a'; CVE record: CWE-125, affected < 0.28.6. Minimum fix f02c970a ('Better bounds checking to fix GHSA-496f-x7cq-cq39', Kevin Backhouse, 2025-07-29) changes only src/epsimage.cpp (+11/-29): replaces the weak checks with overflow-safe 'enforce(posEps <= posEndEps && posEndEps <= size)'; 'enforce(posWmf <= size && sizeWmf <= size - posWmf)'; 'enforce(posTiff <= size && sizeTiff <= size - posTiff)' and enforce(size >= 30), keeping the same error semantics (throw on write path). Role separation preserved: e7373324 'Merge commit from fork' (2025-08-29) is the private security-fork merge whose second parent is exactly f02c970a and whose epsimage.cpp blob is identical (bb4aa330); 4654b52f 'Release Exiv2 version 0.28.6' is the release/vulnerability-boundary commit (GHSA 'fixed in v0.28.6', v0.28.6 tag == 4654b52f, f02c970a is ancestor). The fix 62fb8764 (#73616) replaces the hardcode with resolveSlashCommandAuth(), and its own commit message states 'commandAuthorized was hardcoded to true in the pre-dispatch path'. Origin therefore traces to human-authored bf6f506d, not the AI-marked 5e72e39c.

causal_research.bug_semantics: PluginImportGuard.restore_hidden_modules() restored saved entries, cleared self.hidden_modules, and only then evaluated len(self.hidden_modules), so every restoration audit message reported zero regardless of the number restored. In setup, hide_dangerous_modules() deleted blocked modules from the process-global sys.modules before sys.meta_path.insert(0, import_guard) installed the blocking finder; a thread scheduled between those two operations could re-import a deleted blocked module and retain access to it, bypassing the intended sandbox in a multi-threaded process.

The e588 patch adds the entire PluginImportGuard, stores/deletes blocked sys.modules entries, clears hidden_modules before logging its length, then calls import_guard.hide_dangerous_modules() before sys.meta_path.insert(). Direct parent-tree command `git grep -n -e 'class PluginImportGuard' -e 'restore_hidden_modules' -e 'hide_dangerous_modules' 5f8412ee11ac37e57190d6af4fe02f2cf7f2a5bd -- openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py` returned no matches (exit 1), while the e588 diff is a 131-line addition containing the mechanism. `git cat-file commit e588...` proves the single parent, human author/committer, Claude Code generation line, and Claude Sonnet 4.5 co-author trailer in the BIC commit object. The 85c patch captures count before clear and adds a per-guard threading.Lock; its parent is 0c7418bab59e80a2b40913d8ad8523e6bbab196b. Version checks are unusually important here: `git tag --contains` for both e588 and 85c starts at v1.4.0; v1.3.6 source has no PluginImportGuard, while v1.4.0 contains `_modules_lock` and `logger.debug(f"Restored {count} hidden modules")`. Thus no tagged release in this clone contains the vulnerable interval, contradicting the advisory's literal '<1.4.0' package range; the flaw existed in pre-v1.4.0 branch history and the tagged v1.4.0 tree already contains the direct fix. Finally, inspection of 85c's tree shows hide_dangerous_modules() and sys.meta_path.insert() remain consecutive separate calls; the new private lock is acquired only inside hide/restore and is not acquired by other importing threads. Later cabda2c1dc4842ec737e3ad047fb0e3e4ee129af serializes threading-mode plugin execution and first appears in v1.4.1, but does not make arbitrary process threads honor the per-guard lock.

Its direct parent had no PluginImportGuard, hide_dangerous_modules(), or restore_hidden_modules().

The logging path is deterministic: clear makes the subsequently measured dictionary length zero. The race path follows directly from process-global mutation order: deletion occurs before finder installation, leaving a scheduler-visible interval in which ordinary import machinery has neither the cached module nor the blocking finder. The first-party direct remediation 85c fixes the logging value and declares the threading issue fixed; it precedes the v1.4.0 tag, as does the BIC, so the repository establishes a vulnerable development interval but not a vulnerable tagged version. The race portion should not be treated as conclusively closed by 85c: a lock used only by the same guard's hide/restore methods cannot synchronize unrelated Python imports, and the hide-to-hook ordering remains unchanged.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The unified FastAPI server enabled both JWT-protected modules by default while supplying public, hardcoded 39-character HS256 signing secrets for each module. Startup validation checked only that each secret was at least 32 characters and that the two values differed, so both defaults passed. Because TokenAuth.verify_token() trusted any correctly signed token with the module issuer and the route dependencies returned the attacker-controlled sub claim without requiring that client_id to exist, anyone knowing the source could forge a bearer token for an arbitrary client_id and reach authenticated keyserver upload/revocation and telemetry event APIs.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/security/advisories/GHSA-qc6h-gfjh-7qqg names openssl_encrypt_server/config.py, describes hardcoded defaults passing the >=32 check, states affected <1.4.0, and identifies resolution commit 6090a8e.

git log --all --full-history --reverse -S'keyserver-secret-change-me-min-32-chars' -- openssl_encrypt_server/config.py first returns 8170b3e0be064cdaddbc8ef51c17e21c42d2d3f4; git log -L 175,175:openssl_encrypt_server/config.py 6090a8e^ traces the keyserver default to that commit's creation of the file from /dev/null. The analogous telemetry default is blamed to the same commit.

At 8170b3e0be064cdaddbc8ef51c17e21c42d2d3f4, openssl_encrypt_server/config.py lines 75-83 set keyserver-secret-change-me-min-32-chars and telemetry-secret-change-me-min-32-chars. Each is 39 characters, so the same commit's validate_config() lines 143-159 accepts it under the only per-secret rule, len(secret) >= 32; server.py invokes validate_config(settings) during lifespan startup.

At the BIC, openssl_encrypt_server/core/auth/token.py signs and verifies HS256 JWTs using those configured secrets and validates only the module issuer cryptographically. modules/keyserver/routes.py and modules/telemetry/routes.py use payload.sub as authenticated client_id after best-effort update_last_seen(), without a required client lookup; protected sinks include POST /api/v1/keys, POST /api/v1/keys/{fingerprint}/revoke, and POST /api/v1/telemetry/events.

Direct parent-tree check `git cat-file -e 849da61d5e88aa901c6a8ec70859019a57156363:openssl_encrypt_server/config.py` fails because the path does not exist. The BIC is a one-parent commit, and all-ref content history exposes no earlier member commit containing either vulnerable default, so there is no reconstructable squash decomposition.

`git cat-file commit 8170b3e0be064cdaddbc8ef51c17e21c42d2d3f4` shows human author/committer Tobi plus the exact Claude Code generation line and Claude Sonnet 4.5 Co-Authored-By trailer. Only this BIC commit object was used for AI attribution.

6090a8e329230b5c4b941dcedee4cc4b78bb35a7 directly adds insecure-default marker checks to validate_config() and raises in the default non-debug mode before server startup, matching the first-party resolution. Later commit 8d0d91896ee19ea9c31951b39d72a364b594fd71 additionally removes the defaults, but it is subsequent hardening rather than the first direct fix.

Version cross-check: 8170b3e0be064cdaddbc8ef51c17e21c42d2d3f4 is not an ancestor of v1.3.6, while both it and 6090a8e329230b5c4b941dcedee4cc4b78bb35a7 are ancestors of v1.4.0 (peeled tag commit 768df5cd1910e349509f07a27eeac6951e0003bf). Thus repository tags show the flaw existed on the v1.4 development line and was fixed before the v1.4.0 release boundary; no vulnerable pre-1.4 release tag contains the new unified server path.

potential_fix.approach: Validate webhook.url at write time (POST /api/webhooks and PUT /api/webhooks/:id) and revalidate before every outbound request: parse with the URL constructor, require an allowlisted scheme of http/https only, refuse credentials/other schemes, and reject targets that resolve to loopback (127.0.0.0/8, ::1), RFC1918 space, link-local, or the cloud metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254), before staging the value into sampleWebhooks and before /api/webhooks/:id/test, /api/webhooks/notify, and the lifecycle hooks call fetch(webhook.url).
potential_fix.rationale: The SSRF sink is the backend issuing Node's global fetch to a caller-controlled stored url. Enforcing http(s)-only plus a private/metadata destination block at both registration and fetch time closes the exact relay path used to reach localhost admin ports, RFC1918 services, and the metadata service, while preserving legitimate public webhook delivery.

unpatched.reason: No remediation is recorded in the finding; the audited commit (31dd902) that introduced the outbound fetch is the vulnerable state and the webhook url is accepted and stored with no URL validation, leaving the SSRF unpatched.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated caller creates a gateway secret whose auth_config.api_base is stored without scheme, host, or IP-range checks (_create_gateway_secret). A later POST to /gateway/proxy/{endpoint_name}/{path} (raw_proxy) builds a provider from that secret, then OpenAI-compatible/Anthropic _proxy send an aiohttp POST to append_to_uri_path(api_base, caller_path) and return the upstream body. _validate_webhook_url, which already rejects non-global and metadata addresses for webhooks, is never applied on this path. CreateGatewaySecret is absent from BEFORE_REQUEST_HANDLERS, so any authenticated user including read-only accounts can plant an internal/metadata api_base and read the proxy response. Typed gateway routes already used api_base as a destination before 3.13.0, but this CVE's high-impact

potential_fix.approach: Reject non-http(s) and non-global/metadata api_base values in _create_gateway_secret and _update_gateway_secret by calling _validate_webhook_url (or a gateway-specific equivalent). causal_research.bug_semantics: An untrusted plugin class controls plugin.plugin_id. PluginManager instantiated the class and accepted any nonempty string of at most 50 characters, then propagated that value into PluginSecurityContext. For a plugin without READ_FILES, the sandbox intercepted file operations and called _is_safe_path, but _is_safe_path resolved ~/.openssl_encrypt/plugins/<plugin_id> without validating plugin_id and treated every path with that resolved prefix as allowed. Traversal such as '../../.ssh' therefore changes the purported per-plugin config root to a user directory outside ~/.openssl_encrypt/plugins, allowing the sandboxed plugin to read or write paths there despite lacking general file capability.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Command injection (CWE-74/77) in the MCP server's auto.capture tool. The MCP tool 'auto.capture' (src/index.ts, case 'auto.capture': const commitHash = (args.hash as string) || 'HEAD') forwards the user-supplied hash argument to AutoLearnManager.captureCommit (src/autolearn/AutoLearnManager.ts:253) -> AutoLearner.captureCommit (src/autolearn/AutoLearner.ts:136) -> GitHooksManager.getCommitInfo() (src/autolearn/GitHooksManager.ts). getCommitInfo builds shell commands with the hash interpolated unquoted into a template string passed to execSync: `git show -s --format="..." ${commitHash}`, `git show --stat --format= ${commitHash}`, and `git show --pretty=format: ${commitHash}`. A hash value containing shell metacharacters (e.g. 'HEAD; <cmd>') allows a malicious MCP client to execute arbitrary commands on the host running the MCP server. GHSA-rrf2-j3h9-99wg (alias CVE-2026-19282) rates it CWE-74, CVSS 5.3 (NVD MEDIUM / GHSA LOW), published 2026-08-08, affected version <= f11dc8bcff3ff8cf943a2945f99ff3b0bdc8a6d0. The advisory was filed via issue #21; no fix has been released and the vulnerable code is still present at HEAD. Local attack surface: the MCP server is intended to run on a user's workstation, so the injection is exploited by a malicious/compromised MCP client or by any prompt-induced command in the git-hash parameter.

causal_research.bug_semantics: On a fresh instance with no password configured, check_auth() deliberately admitted every request. POST /api/settings nevertheless accepted the ownership-establishing _set_password pseudo-setting: save_settings() hashed the attacker-chosen value into settings.json as password_hash, turning authentication on. A remote unauthenticated first caller could therefore choose the initial credential, authenticate (and, after the later session-continuity change, receive a session immediately), and lock out the intended operator. The missing invariant was that the unauthenticated disabled-auth state must not permit a non-local client to perform the transition that establishes the first trust root.
evidence: The first-party advisory GHSA-p52p-4vmg-4vq3 (also CVE-2026-49973) identifies versions before v0.51.358, PRs https://github.com/nesquena/hermes-webui/pull/3964 and https://github.com/nesquena/hermes-webui/pull/3973, advisory fix merge https://github.com/nesquena/hermes-webui/commit/1126e541325d401538f6a272a9c024c37d47ae08, and release https://github.com/nesquena/hermes-webui/releases/tag/v0.51.358. PR #3964 documents the attack path: disabled auth admits POST /api/settings, _set_password persists the first password, and the requester can obtain a session and ownership.

Commit-object and patch inspection of b8b62722ec2f6b3cd394737ab409c35650f29ca6 ("feat: Sprint 19 — password auth, security headers, login page") shows the causal additions: api/auth.py added check_auth() with `if not is_auth_enabled(): return True`; api/config.py added password_hash and save_settings() handling that pops _set_password and writes its hash; static/ui.js posted the password to /api/settings; and server.py placed check_auth() before POST routing. This is the smallest public commit that first made the generic settings request establish the initial credential.

Immediate-parent tree verification at 1c6db07c2bef8d53656032a2c39a2385a176c959 found no _set_password, password_hash, check_auth, or HERMES_WEBUI_PASSWORD in api/config.py, api/routes.py, or server.py. The parent api/routes.py did already contain POST /api/settings at lines 307-309 as `return j(handler, save_settings(body))`, but unknown _set_password had no effect. The BIC diff adds the special interpretation and disabled-auth admission; therefore the vulnerable mechanism is absent in the direct parent, not merely moved or renamed.

History cross-check distinguishes the later b8b-like-looking continuity work: 8b857d9efc121586f2ef79ca4b8f92d8ad373b5b (2026-04-14, "login-module-patch: sync to v0.50.36-local.1") added immediate session-cookie issuance after first password setup, but its parent already accepted and persisted _set_password. It amplified convenience for the requester but was not required for takeover, because the requester could authenticate normally using the chosen password. Thus it is not the BIC.

Tag ancestry verifies the introduction boundary exactly: v0.20 resolves to 1c6db07c2bef8d53656032a2c39a2385a176c959, the BIC's immediate parent; merge-base(BIC, v0.20) is that parent. v0.21 resolves to 51bcf8fead50e120fb26d9f7ecf591e6482baf15 and merge-base(BIC, v0.21) is the BIC itself. `git for-each-ref --contains=<BIC> --sort=version:refname` starts at v0.21, so the flaw enters released history there and remains within the advisory's pre-v0.51.358 affected range.

Fix inspection shows direct content commit f2ef2851d389cf7a41308dcf0180d7cfbe446379 has parent 5dceb2993cc0a6bc42697a30d370425db482609a, exactly tag v0.51.357. In api/routes.py it snapshots auth_enabled_before and, before save_settings(), rejects `requested_password and not auth_enabled_before` unless _onboarding_gate_allows() accepts a local/private client or explicit HERMES_WEBUI_ONBOARDING_OPEN opt-in. Its tree f38bf7aca081dfa3ecaf78c90968a5915ebcb83c equals the tree of advisory merge 1126e541325d401538f6a272a9c024c37d47ae08, exactly tag v0.51.358. Ancestry checks confirm the BIC is in v0.51.357 and the direct fix is in v0.51.358.

causal_research.flaw_origin: The optional-password feature commit introduced both halves of the flaw together: api/auth.py made check_auth() return true whenever no password existed, while api/config.py made the already-generic /api/settings save path interpret untrusted _set_password as authority to persist the first password. It added no locality, bootstrap token, or existing-owner check around that transition. A later commit only added automatic cookie issuance; it did not originate the takeover because an attacker could already log in with the password they selected.
causal_research.reasoning: Vulnerability-first reconstruction begins at the ownership transition, not at the later cookie behavior. Before authentication is configured, the middleware intentionally permits all clients. The flaw occurs when that unauthenticated state is combined with the generic settings endpoint's newly added _set_password interpretation: a remote request can create the very credential that subsequent middleware treats as proof of ownership. History of api/config.py and api/routes.py places the first such combination in b8b62722ec2f6b3cd394737ab409c35650f29ca6. Its direct parent has the generic settings route but none of the auth/password pseudo-setting machinery, directly proving parent absence. Later password hardening and the 8b857d9 session-continuity patch retain the already-vulnerable bootstrap and therefore are not smaller origins. Release ancestry independently brackets the lifecycle from v0.20 (parent/absent) to v0.21 (BIC present), through vulnerable v0.51.357, and then to direct guard f2ef2851d389cf7a41308dcf0180d7cfbe446379 and advisory merge/tag v0.51.358. POST /api/v1/keys/register issues a JWT with no prior auth. POST /api/v1/keys/{fingerprint}/revoke then accepts any valid keyserver JWT plus an ML-DSA revocation signature over the fingerprint and sets revoked=True. A different registered client who can produce that signature (i.e., who holds the bundle signing private key) can unpublish another client's key without the original uploader's credentials. causal_research.bug_semantics: BIC 52b69fb (2017-08-25, PR #1972 by Daniel Rampelt/drampelt) is the verified first-write (minimal introducing commit) of the ForwardAuth middleware. auth/forward.go Forward() builds the auth sub-request with forwardReq.Header = r.Header, copying the full client header set verbatim, so a client-supplied X-Forwarded-Prefix is forwarded untouched to the auth server. With trustForwardHeader=false, Traefik's writeHeader rebuilds X-Forwarded-* style headers (X-Forwarded-For/Proto/Port/Host/Uri/Method) but never X-Forwarded-Prefix, leaving an attacker-controlled prefix visible to the auth backend; this can bypass auth when Traefik sits behind a trusted upstream that would otherwise strip/rewrite those headers. Parent f16219f provably lacks any ForwardAuth code (no auth/forward.go, no Forward type), so 52b69fb is a true origin, not a rename. Fix 5e1de22 (2026-04-17, PR #12994 by Julien Salleyron/juliens) changes trustConfig trustForwardHeader to *bool: explicit false now deletes all X-Forwarded-* headers (DeleteXForwardedForHeaders including X-Forwarded-Prefix) before rebuilding the trusted set, while nil preserves legacy behavior. First fixed releases v2.11.43 / v3.6.14 / v3.7.0-rc.2 confirmed by both the official CVE record (CVE-2026-35051) and local git tag --contains of the fix. verdict NOT_AI: BIC is a 2017 pre-LLM human-authored feature commit with no AI markers; fix authored by a named human maintainer. NOT_AI is positively established, not merely inferred from an absent trailer.

causal_research.bug_semantics: MECHANISM: _list_globals backward walker for STACK_GLOBAL collected its two string operands with `for offset in range(1, n)`, a bound that can never inspect opcode index 0; a crafted pickle whose operand stack includes an opcode at index 0 yields len(values)!=2 and raises ValueError during scanning, producing a detection bypass. LINEAGE (independently verified in local clone mmaitre314__picklescan): initial scanner c1d5abdcc7 (2022-09-04, Matthieu Maitre) handled STACK_GLOBAL with fixed ops[n-2]/ops[n-1] SHORT_BINUNICODE reads only. BIC 18c978e9 (2022-09-05, single parent 9c31e179 confirmed via rev-list) rewrote _list_globals for multiple-pickle support and first wrote the range(1,n) walker; the diff minus-side and 9c31e179:scanner.py show the parent has no range loop (fixed-index form only), and c1d5abd is an ancestor of 9c31e179, so the off-by-one bound originates in this BIC, not in the initial scanner. Between 2022 and 2025 the walker body grew opcode-family support (MEMOIZE/PUT/GET resolution, UNICODE/BINUNICODE/BINUNICODE8 string handling) through later named-human commits (Matthieu Maitre, Luc Georges, quasar098; e.g. e99f3ae PUT support, aeb7641 memoized values, 40001cd INST); this secondary history is preserved separately and the CVE boundary stays the range(1,n) bound first written in the BIC. FIX: 58983e1c (PR #46, 2025-08-09, authored by Matthieu Maitre, GitHub-committer squash; only commit in local history changing the loop text per -S search) changes the bound to range(1, n+1) and adds STRING/BINSTRING/SHORT_BINSTRING to the recognized string family, closing the index-0 blind spot; tag v0.0.27 == 58983e1c and v0.0.26 == 2a8383cf (the OSV-listed alternate commit, a README/setup.cfg image-link change, still vulnerable), so first fixed release boundary is 0.0.27. causal_research.bug_semantics: Module/advisory: picklescan failed to flag a pickle REDUCE payload calling asyncio.unix_events._UnixSubprocessTransport._start (GHSA-q77w-mwjj-7mqx). Mechanism: from scanner inception the deny-list (_suspicious_globals/_unsafe_globals) is looked up by exact g.module with value '*' or a name set, so a global whose module string is the submodule 'asyncio.unix_events' never matched any entry and was never dangerous-flagged (inception build did not even warn on unlisted modules). Verified lineage: BIC c1d5abd (Implement Pickle scanner, 2022-09-04) is the first write of src/picklescan/scanner.py and of the deny-list/exact-module lookup (git show --name-status: scanner.py is A; GLOBAL/STACK_GLOBAL parsing and exact _suspicious_globals.get(g[0]) matching exist in this commit); parent 6a76b8c (2022-09-03) contains only boilerplate (.gitignore, LICENSE, README.md, conda.yaml, requirements.txt, setup.cfg) with no scanner code, so no vulnerable detection existed in the parent and the BIC is the minimal inception of the omission. git log -S asyncio over src/picklescan/scanner.py returns exactly b1d7c63 (add 'asyncio': '*', 2024-09-25, PR #30 by Luc Georges), 1931c2d (fix), 28a7b4e (generalization); no pre-fix revision ever contained an asyncio.unix_events entry or submodule-prefix matching, so the archive-candidate BIC b1d7c638 is only a later deny-list expansion whose exact-module '*' semantics (unchanged since inception, verified in scanner.py at b1d7c638: unsafe_filter = _unsafe_globals.get(g.module)) never covered submodule-addressed globals - it neither introduced nor worsened the gap, and its parent 15c0dbd3 likewise has no asyncio entry. Fix: 1931c2d (Missing detection when calling Python functions (#49), 2025-08-26, Matthieu Maitre) is a 10-GHSA multi-advisory commit; the direct per-module repair for this advisory is the added entry 'asyncio.unix_events': {'_UnixSubprocessTransport._start'}. Release boundary: v0.0.29..v0.0.30 contains exactly 1931c2d and git tag --contains 1931c2d starts at v0.0.30, so first fixed release is v0.0.30 and all earlier releases (scanner inception v0.0.1..v0.0.29) are affected (<0.0.30 per advisory). Follow-up 28a7b4e (v0.0.31) generalizes the fix (top-level '*' deny entries propagate to submodules) and removes the explicit entry, preserving coverage. causal_research.bug_semantics: CONFIRMED: origin 4fa058f3 introduced the reaction operation without the visibility policy required by the same change, not by carrying an earlier authorization omission. causal_research.bug_semantics: Mechanism: NimbusJwtDecoder.withIssuerLocation / NimbusReactiveJwtDecoder.withIssuerLocation only derived a JWK-set builder (fetch discovery config, validate provider-configuration issuer against metadata, default algorithms), with an empty Nimbus claims verifier and no issuer-claim validator attached to the built decoder; build() therefore accepted any JWT signed by a key in the issuer's discovered JWK set with a missing or different iss claim (issuer trust confusion). Lineage (verified in local git): BIC 76eba9bd (2023-04-12, author/committer Josh Cummings, message 'Add withIssuerLocation / Closes gh-10309') is the true first write of both APIs; parent 9ee8202 has zero withIssuerLocation occurrences repo-wide, and diff shows both method families introduced with A/M file states plus JwkSetUriJwtDecoderBuilder refactor. Same commit rewrote JwtDecoders.fromIssuerLocation to compose the new builder and then explicitly decoder.setJwtValidator(JwtValidators.createDefaultWithIssuer(issuer)), demonstrating issuer-bound validation was known-required on that path but was omitted inside the new public builder API the advisory covers. Fix: 68b820ed (2026-04-15, 'Check Issuer with Issuer Provided', Josh Cummings, single parent 44d32815, atomic 4-file/62-insertion change) adds .validator(JwtValidators.createDefaultWithIssuer(issuer)) on the withIssuerLocation factories, defaults builder validator to JwtValidators.createDefault(), and applies decoder.setJwtValidator(this.validator) in build(). Release boundary: first OSS tags containing the fix are 6.5.10 (2026-04-20) and 7.0.5; 6.5.9 and 7.0.4 verified NOT to contain 68b820ed. BIC first shipped in 6.1.0-RC1/6.1.0, so the flaw exists from API introduction (6.1.0) through 6.5.9/7.0.4. AI evidence (positive): named human maintainer Josh Cummings authored and committed the BIC in April 2023 for human feature request gh-10309 ('Add NimbusJwtDecoder#withIssuerLocation'); commit has no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with/bot trailer; repo calibration over 2022-11..2023-08 (1255 commits) shows zero AI contribution trailers (only human GitHub co-author entries), while 2025-2026 commits do carry AI trailers (e.g. two Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6), so absence of a trailer is meaningful against a calibrated convention. Verified lineage: local clone openclaw/openclaw (114k commits, no shallow). BIC a4c68d890 (author AkosCz, 2026-02-09 22:05:42 -0600, verified via GitHub commit page + .patch; parents:[c92c3ad224]) is the first write of runGeminiSearch/resolveRedirectUrl/REDIRECT_TIMEOUT: main parent 3f03cdea56 and PR parent c92c3ad224 web-search.ts both contain zero occurrences (830-line parent file checked via raw.githubusercontent), so parent is vulnerability-free. BIC landed on main 2026-02-23 as GitHub squash merge 3a3c2da916 (committer GitHub, squash aggregates several PR member commits). Intermediate hardening 5eb72ab769 (2026-02-24, Peter Steinberger) wrapped resolveRedirectUrl in fetchWithSsrFGuard but with TRUSTED_NETWORK_SSRF_POLICY={dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork:true} (trusted-network model), leaving private-network reachability - matches advisory wording 'private-network-allowing SSRF policy'; that commit is not the origin because the raw redirect-following HEAD fetch already reached private networks without any guard. causal_research.bug_semantics: CAUSE: GitProxy (BIC 8cec7591, 'wip', 2020-05-31) parses the client receive-pack ref-update line into commitFrom/commitTo (parsePush.js: action.setCommit(messageParts[0].substr(4), messageParts[1])) and writePack.js pipes the ENTIRE client request body ('input: req.body') to 'git receive-pack'. Nothing validates that every commit object in the client pack is reachable from the advertised newOid, so extra commits in the pack are written to the upstream repo and remain fetchable by direct SHA even though no branch points at them (silent exfiltration; GHSA-v98g-8rqx-g93g, CWE-345). BIC/PARENT CONTRAST: parent 01d337a7 has no proxy/processors or writePack path at all; BIC introduces the proxy push chain and this gap in one 'wip' commit, so 8cec7591 is the true BIC and the parent contains none of the vulnerable receive-pack/audit pipeline. MINIMAL FIX: the initial 'feat: add check for hidden commits' 9c1449f4 (Fabio Vincenzi, 2025-05-16) was INCOMPLETE ON ITS OWN: it never landed on main before the security merge (merge-base --is-ancestor 9c1449f4 d4d9239a = false), it only detected pack commits outside oldOid..newOid, and it did not persist newIdxFiles or fix parsePush. The terminal security change is fork-merge a620a2f33 ('Merge commit from fork', Thomas Cooper, 2025-07-30, parents d4d9239a + 60e77d1c): (1) writePack.ts now snapshots .idx files before/after receive-pack and stores action.newIdxFiles; (2) chain.ts inserts checkHiddenCommits between writePack and checkIfWaitingAuth; (3) the rewritten checkHiddenCommits.ts fails the push when any commit in the new idx files is outside the introduced rev-list range; (4) parsePush (394-line diff, incl. 93a6123c capability parsing, co-authored Thomas Cooper) and getMissingData harden the same surface. 9c1449f4 and the fork-branch line it heads (1fd86acb idx tracking, 334c967e UpdatedRef/newIdxFiles in Action, 00287432 empty-branch-push guard, 93a6123c parsePush capability parsing) are the incomplete-first-fix boundary that the merge folds in; 12fce21a (1.19.2 package.json bump) is a release marker, not a fix. The merged security state first ships in v1.19.2 (git tag --contains a620a2f33 -> v1.19.2; GHSA: affected <= 1.19.1, patched 1.19.2 and 2.0.0). AI EVIDENCE: no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with/Copilot/Cursor/Claude/GPT marker on BIC 8cec7591 or anywhere in the last 40 security-fix commits on the fork branch; BIC author == committer grovesy (Paul Groves). Missing markers are absence-of-positive-evidence only and cannot alone support NOT_AI; the verdict_before label is carried forward unconfirmed, and the independent git evidence neither confirms nor denies AI authorship.

round13_research.bug_semantics: Zalo zalouser personal-channel monitor accepts non-numeric allowFrom/groupAllowFrom entries and, at startup, binds them to whatever friend currently has that displayName (or group has that name). Because display names are mutable by users, an attacker can rename their account to an allowlisted name and so be resolved into the numeric allowlist, passing isSenderAllowed admission for impersonation/spoofing (CWE-290).
evidence: CVE-2026-53857 / GHSA-8c59-hr4w-qg69: Zalo allowFrom could bind to mutable display names, CWE-290, CVSS 8.1.

Source-to-sink chain: allowFrom/groupAllowFrom raw name -> startup name-to-ID binding -> isSenderAllowed senderId admission -> agent processes message.

Zalo zalouser personal channel resolves non-numeric allowFrom / groupAllowFrom config entries to friend/group IDs by matching mutable displayName at startup, then merges the matched numeric IDs into the allowlist (extensions/zalouser/src/monitor.ts monitorZalouserProvider startup block).

An attacker who can change their Zalo display name to an allowlisted name captures that allowlist slot, spoofing an allowed sender (CWE-290, self-descriptive vulnerability).

causal_research.bug_semantics: Provenance is settled by the tree: every traced call site passes password-derived material (the user password itself when no KDF is configured, sha256(password+salt), the running hash-chain buffer seeded with password+salt(+pepper), or an Argon2/PBKDF2 output over that password), and the per-encryption random salt is inside the IKM in every one of those paths, so two encryptions never share an IKM and the multi-target amortisation premise the advisory relies on does not hold; HKDF with salt=None is RFC 5869 section 3.1-defined behaviour, not an out-of-spec construct. The vendor's own fix for the linked advisory changed CryptoKey.derive_subkey and explicitly retained salt=None in _normalize_bytes as required for deterministic decryption (random salt there would break decryption), so the deterministic normalization is intended design, and the residual weakness is a hardening/margin item with no violated security premise. Attribution fails independently of that: the supplied candidate BIC 1dfb5f1 contains neither function at all (git grep exit=1 at that tree) and its diff touches six unrelated files, so it cannot be the introducer. The first write is 4776a7ce (2026-01-09, Tobi), whose commit object carries no Co-Authored-By or Claude trailer and whose parent tree has zero occurrences of the static info string; the only AI-marked commit in the chain is 79ec749b, which copied the identical HKDF parameters into the new parallel_kdf.py file under a commit-wide 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5' trailer, which is commit-level co-authorship over a re-implementation of the human-written function and not per-line provenance. display_hunks.annotation: The auto-load path arrived with a sandbox-root guard and nothing else: the loader's options hold a byte limit and a sandbox root, so there was no workspace-only decision to make on this path.

The fix gives the loader a workspace-only flag, rejects any resolved path outside the allowed root before the file is read, and passes the flag from the auto-load caller, so the setting now reaches prompt and history images.
The flag is derived from the effective agent configuration, which is how a per-agent workspace-only setting reaches the image auto-load path the same way it already reached the file tools.

steps.detail: The vision feature added the auto-load path that scans a prompt and earlier turns for image references, loads the files and attaches them to the request; its only sandbox guard compared paths to a sandbox root, and the workspace-only setting that the file tools later gained was never consulted here.

steps.detail: The loader now takes the workspace-only flag from the effective agent configuration, rejects any resolved path that falls outside the allowed root, and skips the image; the new tests exercise a prompt reference and a history reference against a sandbox that mounts a directory outside the workspace.

steps.detail: The hardening pass that removed expansion from clone URLs added an expand_vars switch to the shared URL helper and turned it off only on the clone path, leaving the permissive default in place for every other caller.
steps.title: AI change

steps.detail: The completing change passes expand_vars=False from the remote creation and submodule add call sites, so those stored URLs keep their literal ${...} text instead of carrying substituted secrets.

code_evidence.summary: An AI-assisted change stopped environment expansion on clone URLs but left the same expansion in the remote and submodule callers, so a URL passed to create_remote or add could embed the hosting process's secrets and carry them to the attacker's host.

attempted_remediation.changed: Added an expand_vars switch to polish_url and opted the clone path out of expansion (the clone URL and the stored origin are passed with expand_vars=False).
attempted_remediation.missed: Left the remote path on the expanding default: git/remote.py still called Git.polish_url(url), so Remote.add() and Repo.create_remote() expanded environment variables.

final_closure.closed: Flipped the two remaining callers, git/remote.py and git/objects/submodule/base.py, to polish_url(url, expand_vars=False).

ir_chain.original_mechanism: Git.polish_url() ran os.path.expandvars() over every URL it was handed, so a caller-supplied clone URL carrying $NAME or ${NAME} tokens had the hosting process's environment expanded into it.
ir_chain.original_sink: Git.polish_url() in git/cmd.py, reached from Repo.clone_from()
ir_chain.residual_bypass: A remote URL added through Remote.add() or Repo.create_remote() still had environment variables expanded into it, so a hosting-process secret could be sent to the attacker-named host.

display_hunks.annotation: The Copilot-coauthored TypeScript runtime created a plain Nunjucks environment and sent prepared host values directly to renderString. Attacker-controlled templates could traverse constructor and prototype properties and invoke functions in the host Node.js process.

Restoring the original runtime hooks in finally confines those guards to this render operation.

The vulnerable sink previously passed prepared host values straight to the unrestricted environment. This call-site replacement makes both input sanitization and the guarded Nunjucks runtime mandatory on the actual render path.

display_hunks.annotation: Successful trusted-proxy authentication made the pairing decision return skip and let a connection without device identity pass, so the operator scopes a client declared were trusted before pairing bound them.
The handler derived the trusted-proxy predicate from authentication success alone and fed it into both the pairing decision and the missing-device-identity check.
The repair deletes the early return and the scope exemption, so a proxy-authenticated connection must pair before its scopes are honored and unbound scopes are cleared again.
Device-token issuance is now gated on the absence of trusted-proxy authentication, so a live proxy connection cannot obtain a token without a paired device identity.

steps.detail: The change that let trusted-proxy authentication skip device pairing added the proxy arm to the pairing decision, the early return that made any trusted-proxy Control UI connection pairing-bypass eligible, and the matching allow in the missing-device-identity check. Its message ends with a Cursor co-author trailer.
steps.title: AI change

steps.detail: The repair removes the pairing bypass and the scope exemption, clears self-declared scopes when no device identity exists, and stops issuing device tokens on the trusted-proxy path, so pairing now comes before proxy-scoped access.
steps.title: Fix

code_evidence.summary: Openclaw 2026.2.24 through 2026.5.12 treated successful trusted-proxy authentication as enough to skip device pairing, so a restricted or unpaired Control UI client could keep the operator scopes it declared on connect and use admin-only gateway calls on that connection; 2026.5.18 requires pairing first.

attempted_remediation.changed: Let a successful trusted-proxy authentication skip device pairing: shouldSkipControlUiPairing returned true, the missing-device-identity check answered allow, and the scopes the client declared on connect survived.
attempted_remediation.missed: Dropped the pairing baseline for scope binding on the whole trusted-proxy path; the role gate added two days later (ec45c317, requiring role === 'operator') narrowed the bypass and left the same pre-pairing path open for operator-role sessions.

final_closure.closed: Removed the proxy pairing bypass, required pairing before proxy-scoped access, cleared unbound scopes and stopped issuing device tokens without a paired device identity.

ir_chain.original_mechanism: A Control UI session behind a trusted reverse proxy still had to complete device pairing before its requested scopes were trusted, which is the behaviour issue #25293 asked to change.
ir_chain.original_sink: websocket connect policy in src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-policy.ts and message-handler.ts
ir_chain.residual_bypass: An unpaired operator-role Control UI session behind a trusted proxy kept the scopes it declared on connect and could exercise admin-gated gateway calls; v2026.5.12 still carried the pairing-skip early return, the scope exemption and the allow.

code_evidence.summary: An AI-assisted change added option screening for revision traversal but wired it only into the iterator that walks commits, so the counting method on the same commit kept forwarding a file-overwriting option to git and could blank any file the caller named.

attempted_remediation.changed: Added unsafe_git_rev_options with --output and -o, the allow_unsafe_options parameter and the check_unsafe_options call inside Commit.iter_items, as part of the same four-file hardening pass that guarded Repo.archive and git.ls_remote.

display_hunks.annotation: The imported plugin builds the mention-stripping pattern from the mention name and the mention key themselves, and its caller runs that helper on every inbound message, so sender-controlled metadata becomes pattern syntax.

The fix escapes metacharacters in the mention name and key before the pattern is compiled, so the metadata is matched as literal text and a hostile name can no longer change the pattern or its running time.

steps.detail: The imported plugin removed incoming mentions with a regular expression built from the raw mention name and key, so message metadata became pattern syntax rather than literal text.

steps.detail: The helper escapes regular-expression metacharacters in both the mention name and the mention key before compiling the pattern, matching the escaping the neighbouring mention helper already used.
