steps.detail: The change that moved code execution into a subprocess also wrote the list of forbidden attribute names, and that list never named the attribute that hands back the builtins module.
steps.title: AI change

steps.detail: The default sandbox mode skips the older text-pattern list, so the guard was the static syntax scan alone, and every release from the first subprocess-mode version through 1.6.39 shipped that list as written.
steps.title: Reachable window

steps.detail: The repair adds the leaking attribute and the helper call to the blocked sets, screens calls written as attribute access, and runs the same syntax check at the entry to sandboxed execution, so the proof is refused before it starts.
steps.title: Fix

code_evidence.summary: The execute_code tool's subprocess sandbox screened submitted programs against a fixed list of dangerous attribute names, and that list omitted the attribute that exposes the live builtins module, so a short program could still run operating system commands as the server user.

attempted_remediation.changed: Added the _execute_code_sandboxed subprocess wrapper with a blocked_attrs screen and a restricted builtins dictionary, and made sandbox mode the default.
attempted_remediation.missed: The attribute screen listed the usual dunder names but not __self__, so a bound method still leaked its module: print.__self__ handed the snippet the builtins module.

final_closure.closed: Blocks __self__ and vars and validates the snippet's AST before execution ('Security Error: Access to attribute __self__ is restricted').

ir_chain.original_mechanism: execute_code handed caller-supplied Python to the interpreter with no sandbox wrapper and no attribute screen, so a snippet could reach interpreter internals such as the builtins module.
ir_chain.residual_bypass: print.__self__ reached the builtins module through the attribute screen, so a sandboxed snippet could rebuild imports and leave the sandbox.

steps.detail: Every interpolated value now passes through html.escape into a local named safe before it reaches the page, and the application name is no longer displayed at all, which removes the injection points instead of filtering particular characters.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The withdrawn report alleged that an attacker could begin an OAuth sign-in, reach an OTP challenge, alter the factor strategy in the attempt request, and complete authentication without the correct code. A browser can always alter its request, so the alleged bypass would require the Frontend API server to accept a factor that was not valid for the prepared sign-in state. The CNA subsequently rejected CVE-2025-63700 after determining that it was not a security issue.
evidence: Advisory disposition re-check: https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2025-63700 currently returns cveMetadata.state=REJECTED, dateRejected=2025-12-23, and the CNA reason 'Further investigation showed that it was not a security issue.' The GitHub advisory API remains stale: https://api.github.com/advisories/GHSA-3mm3-wfpv-q85g still says @clerk/clerk-js <= 5.88.0 but reports first_patched_version=null and withdrawn_at=null. At @clerk/clerk-js 5.88.0 the public SDK only sends the selected strategy and entered code to the Frontend API; the authentication decision and factor-to-state binding are server-side. The relevant client transport predates 5.88.0, and the authoritative rejection establishes no vulnerable server behavior or repository-local origin.
causal_research.reasoning: Vulnerability-first analysis ends without a BIC. The alleged security decision is server-side, the public client merely serializes caller-controlled factor parameters, release 5.88.0 did not add that transport, and the CNA affirmatively rejected the CVE as not a security issue. The earliest public-history appearance is a wholesale source import whose direct parent lacks the file; protocol forbids treating imports or aggregates as the smallest real BIC. With no verified vulnerable lines, no BIC/direct-parent absence proof for a flaw, and no patched version or fix, EVIDENCE_GAP is gate-complete. Bundle GHSA-3mm3-wfpv-q85g matches: package @clerk/clerk-js, range <=5.88.0, first_patched_version null, withdrawn_at null; no Clerk-owned repo advisory or patched clerk-js release is cited.
round11_research.flaw_origin: The claimed bypass never became a demonstrated clerk-js defect. MITRE first recorded a Supplier dispute (irreproducible; an OAuth-flow bug would live in the backend, not in the clerk-js frontend). On 2025-12-23 the CNA withdrew CVE-2025-63700 as not a security issue. Clerk's public security history independently states the filing was a disputed external report that NVD rejected and that it was never a real vulnerability. No BIC or fix is required.
round11_research.reasoning: Vulnerability-first review of CVE-2025-63700 / GHSA-3mm3-wfpv-q85g shows the advisory never established a reproducible clerk-js flaw. The only technical story is a third-party README claiming an attacker could mutate an OTP verification request across authentication strategies (email OTP, TOTP, OAuth) and finish sign-in without a valid code because the backend did not re-validate the stage. That writeup has no exploit artifacts, and the GHSA lists no patched version, which is inconsistent with a confirmed client-library bug. MITRE then recorded the Supplier dispute: the issue could not be reproduced, and an OAuth authentication-flow failure would be fixed in Clerk's backend rather than in clerk-js (frontend only). On 2025-12-23 the CNA withdrew the CVE as not a security issue; NVD and CVE.org now show REJECTED with that exact reason. Clerk's own published security history repeats that this filing was investigated, withdrawn, and never a real vulnerability. GitHub's GHSA remains un-withdrawn (withdrawn_at null); that field is not authoritative against the CVE.org/CNA rejection. Under AUDIT-PROTOCOL, withdrawn/rejected advisories that are not a security issue are FALSE_POSITIVE, not NOT_AI. FALSE_POSITIVE does not require a BIC, so introducer_sha, introducer_parent, fix_sha, and direct_fix_sha are null and AI markers were not evaluated on a commit object.

causal_research.parent_absence_evidence: The root commit 967c66b created Dockerfile without a USER directive; its parent is the empty root boundary. git show 17a119fe adds groupadd/useradd, chown, and USER ciguard. Both the root commit and the fix are human-authored; Claude appears only on the later batch fix.
causal_research.remaining_gap: Attribution is project/slice scoped: PRD.md in the BIC commit discloses the Claude Code sessions that delivered the defective artifacts, but no commit-object marker exists on the root commit and hunk-level authorship is not recoverable, so ai_hunk records NARROW.
